Even complete access to transformed memory stores leaves an accuracy gap relative to raw evidence, highlighting the importance of preserving raw information. These findings challenge the necessity of complex agentic memory for the evaluated conversation tasks and establish naive RAG as an essential baseline.

title: Primal-Dual Representation Learning for Low-Rank Constrained MDPs
abstract: Representation learning has substantially improved the efficiency of unconstrained continuous-state Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), but its extension to Constrained MDPs (CMDPs) is difficult because the transition representation must be learned while constraint violation is controlled. In this paper, we study representation learning for low-rank CMDPs with continuous state spaces, and propose REP-PD-TEG for the soft cumulative-violation setting. In the feature learning period, the algorithm interacts with the environment using a decaying-$ε$-greedy mixture execution policy, and uses the collected samples to learn transition features by maximum likelihood. Based on the learned features, it constructs uncertainty bonuses and plans with an optimistic Lagrangian objective to obtain the return policy. We prove regret and soft-violation guarantees for the return policies, and quantify the influence of the decaying-$ε$-greedy exploration. In particular, REP-PD-TEG achieves the optimal $\widetilde O(\sqrt K)$ return policy bound, and gives a $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ overall sample bound when exploratory actions are charged. For the stricter hard cumulative violation, where feasibility must be verified episode by episode, we propose REP-PD-H-TEG. It plans under a bonus-corrected lower-confidence utility certificate with the learned representation, and performs a stabilized dual search to obtain the return policy, yielding regret and hard-violation bounds. Together, these results give the first theoretically guaranteed representation-learning method for low-rank continuous-state CMDPs with both soft cumulative guarantees and certified hard-violation control.

title: Reconfigurable Free-Space Optical Interconnects
abstract: Free-space optical interconnects can support many low-data-rate channels while avoiding the cost, energy consumption, and packaging constraints of optical waveguide- or fiber-based systems that are widely used today. We propose a free-space optical interconnect system based on reconfigurable micromirror arrays, and show that it scales favorably due to its two-dimensional scaling. We discuss the channel count scaling model, compare our demonstration with theory, and project a channel count above 10,000 to achieve 100 Tbps with slow channels (e.g., <10 Gbps). In a proof-of-concept system with a piston-motion micromirror array, we demonstrate nine channels that are simultaneously optimized. The optimization enables -21.7 dB of average worst-case crosstalk for a channel pitch equal to twice the beam radius, a smaller channel spacing than that required in flat tip-tilt mirrors. The optimization flow is further investigated for different channel spacings, simultaneous illumination, and different numbers of outputs, which generally achieve smaller worst-case crosstalk than the flat tip-tilt mirror case. Overall, the work demonstrates the advantage of piston-motion micromirrors in the proposed optical interconnects.

title: Can Loan Processors and Underwriters Spot AI-Edited Statements? An Empirical Study
abstract: AI-assisted editing can produce loan documents that preserve familiar issuer layouts while changing the applicant's identity. We investigated whether experienced underwriters and loan processors identify such forgeries in first-pass, document-only review. Three practitioners recruited through Upwork each received one applicant package drawn from 134 forged PDFs derived from 47 genuine financial documents supplied with full consent. The edits preserved amounts, dates and balances; identifier inconsistencies introduced by the pipeline were knowingly retained before distribution. Reviewers were not told that files had been altered and returned 132 file-level judgements. Checking their explanations against the originals yielded 14 edit-supported concerns (10.6%): 12 Suspicious judgements and two Insufficient information judgements. All supported concerns involved identifier disagreements within or across documents, and no reported visual cue identified an actual edit. Thus, approximately one in ten judgements contained evidence of the forgery, despite known inconsistencies remaining in the files. These observations motivate evaluating consistency checks and independent source verification alongside human review. With three reviewer-package pairs and no genuine-file controls, the findings describe this exploratory setting rather than population-wide detection accuracy.

title: RAIN: Agentic Proof Generation for Rocq-based Software Verification
abstract: Interactive theorem provers can provide strong correctness guarantees for software, but constructing the proofs remains a challenging and labor-intensive task. Inspired by the recent progress of modern coding agents, we present RAIN, a lightweight proof-specialized agent for Rocq proof generation. RAIN augments an LLM with proof engineering capabilities, including repository exploration, iterative refinement, and checker feedback. This design allows the agent to retrieve lemmas autonomously, revise complete proof scripts instead of isolated tactics, and iteratively refine its proof strategy using enriched proof-state information. Evaluated on a subset from CoqStoq, RAIN shows substantial improvements over the existing baselines, achieving over 90% prove success rate with at least 24.7% improvements. We also compare with general-purpose coding agents, the results show that RAIN maintains comparable prove success rate but with significant lower cost.

title: AgentDP: Towards Automated Model Deployment for Heterogeneous Embedded AI Applications
abstract: This paper presents AgentDP, which aims to deploy pre-trained AI models on heterogeneous embedded devices by fully automating model optimization and adaptation (O&A) with Large Language Model (LLM) agents. AgentDP not only significantly reduces human effort via automation but also enhances model inference efficacy by integrating LLMs with device-specific domain knowledge. To deliver a robust automation framework, AgentDP develops novel solutions to address three key technical challenges: 1) To help users elicit clear requirements, we propose a user requirement standardization module; 2) To mitigate the execution environment mismatch between AI models and heterogeneous embedded devices, we design an operator-aware model partition paradigm that enables different parts of the model to be efficiently executed on distinct inference engines. 3) To avoid re-searching optimization hyperparameters for new tasks, we propose a configuration reuse module that heuristically retrieves previous hyperparameter configurations for efficient reuse. Extensive experiments demonstrate that by fully automating the entire O&A process, AgentDP reduces entire model adaptation time by up to 80% compared with manual O&A while achieving higher task accuracy (more than 13% on average) than the baselines. Additionally, a comprehensive user study also exhibits the robust generalizability of AgentDP in adapting to different user requirements for heterogeneous embedded devices.

title: A simple proof of unitary parallelization via port-based teleportation
abstract: Port-based teleportation (PBT) is a variant of quantum teleportation that does not require corrections on the teleported state: starting with $N$ shared EPR states, Alice can teleport a qudit to Bob by performing a measurement on her system and informing Bob which of his $N$ `ports' to retrieve the state, up to infidelity decaying with $N$. Existing quantum circuits of PBT rely on representation theory tools and the mixed Schur transform. In this note, we report an elementary efficient circuit for PBT, which has depth $\operatorname{polylog}(N,d)$. As a corollary, this gives a simple proof that all $n$-qubit unitaries can be parallelized to $\operatorname{poly}(n)$ depth, recovering a recent result due to Nehoran--Slote--Yuen and OpenAI.

title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.

title: Abstract Priorities, Concrete Rewards: How Stated Preferences Relate to What People Reward in AI Responses
abstract: AI assistants built on large language models (LLMs) are trained on human feedback and increasingly personalized to users' stated preferences. Yet how closely these preferences reflect what people reward in responses remains unclear. We compare stated and revealed preferences in the public PRISM dataset, in which 1,396 participants reported how much seven response attributes mattered to them and then rated 29,347 responses from 21 LLMs. Among responses to the same prompt, features the survey never asked about, such as response length, formatting and refusal language, were at least as strongly associated with ratings as text proxies of the surveyed attributes. Whether stated priorities matched ratings depended on how attributes were measured: participants who prioritized an attribute favoured responses from models that others perceived as strong on it, but not responses that scored higher on text proxies for it. Written feedback was more telling: participants who asked for shorter answers, even in earlier conversations, gave length less weight in their ratings, and those asking for longer answers gave it more. Their relative priorities over the surveyed attributes, however, did not predict this weight. Reasons given for choices reflected perceived attributes more than measured features. Participants also differed stably in how much they weighted several concrete features, especially length, but with a median of 6 conversations per participant, these weights were estimated poorly. The largest gain from personal information in predicting held-out choices was 0.13 percentage points, compared with 1.11 for a stronger pooled model. Stated priorities thus track perceived attributes of AI responses but say little about the concrete features that ratings reward, a distinction that matters for preference elicitation and AI personalization.

title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
abstract: Solution-phase synthesis of monolayer hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites is constrained by rapid out-of-plane crystal growth, uncontrolled nucleation, and strong interlayer aggregation, yielding flakes of only a few μm. We introduce a steric-engineering ternary-solvent growth strategy to synthesize monolayer and few-layer A2MX4 hybrid perovskites with exceptionally large surface areas. By combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive, out-of-plane stacking is suppressed. Using (PEA)2CuCl4 as a model system, monolayers with lateral areas exceeding 1000 μm2 are achieved, representing a massive dimensional increase over conventional methods. Molecular dynamics and quantum-chemical calculations show that longer-chain alcohols reorganize precursor solvation, while solvent volatility prolongs edge-mediated precursor transport during annealing. This strategy demonstrates universal applicability across diverse organic spacer cations (PEA+, F-PEA+, PentA+), metal centers (Cu2+, Mn2+, Pb2+), and halides (Cl-, Br-, I-). The large lateral dimensions enable direct, solvent-free electrical contact fabrication via physical shadow masking, bypassing chemical degradation from solvents used in conventional lithography. Planar devices fabricated from isolated ultrathin (PEA)2PbI4 channels exhibit ultra-low dark currents down to the 10^-15 - 10^-13 A range, enabling femtowatt-to-picowatt static power consumption, ~ 0.2 pW at 5 V, a 250-fold reduction relative to drop-cast films, while maintaining a high light-to-dark current ratio of 4.3 x 102. This work establishes precise steric and solvation control as a paradigm for scalable, compositionally diverse, low-static-power monolayer 2D perovskite optoelectronics.

title: Scaling Laws for Generative Reward Models
abstract: We study generative reward models (GenRMs) as online preference providers for policy optimization in creative writing. Across Qwen3 reward-model sizes from 0.6B to 14B, Thinking judges trained with GRPO have higher static Gold-label accuracy than Answer-Only judges trained with SFT. This ranking often reverses when the judges train policies through online DPO: Answer-Only rewarders yield higher peak and top-five-average policy Elo in seven of eight matched settings under a fixed, learned 32B Gold evaluator. Intermediate Thinking-judge checkpoints can also outperform later, more statically accurate checkpoints as rewarders. Sweeps over rewarder size, policy size, training duration and DPO regularization show substantial benefits from reward-model capacity, including judges larger than the policy. We analyze trajectories with evaluator-specific Elo arenas, conditional match-resampling intervals and descriptive scaling fits. These results demonstrate an evaluator-rewarder gap in the studied pipelines: fixed-distribution judging accuracy does not determine downstream optimization quality. The comparison changes judge-training objective as well as response format, and the main ranking is conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result. A limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.

title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca$_2$CuO$_2$Cl$_2$, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic $4a_0 \times 2a_0$ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed $4a_0$ electronic structures.

title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
abstract: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{λ,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_μ$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

title: Adaptive Deadline- and Energy-Aware Caching Algorithms in Dynamic Multi-UAV Edge Networks
abstract: Content caching via unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) becomes one of the solutions to maintain content delivery when terrestrial infrastructure is unavailable or disrupted. However, existing caching approaches often focus primarily on cache-hit performance or average delivery delay, without jointly addressing spatially heterogeneous and time-varying demand, content-specific deadlines, and uneven communication-energy consumption across UAVs. To address these challenges, we formulate a dynamic deadline- and energy-aware cache placement and replacement problem that jointly considers deadline misses, UAV-side communication energy, and inter-UAV energy imbalance. To achieve this, we first develop deadline- and energy-aware UBAC (DE-UBAC), an interpretable hierarchical rule-based realization that incorporates deadline-aware prioritization, cooperative placement, energy-aware coordination, and cache-update cost. However, predefined priorities and thresholds limit its adaptability under dynamically coupled network conditions. We therefore propose GRU-assisted Deadline- and Energy-aware Proximal Policy Optimization (GRU-DEPPO), which combines local and global GRU-based temporal representations with a centralized PPO actor-critic for adaptive cache placement and replacement. Simulation results show that GRU-DEPPO achieves the lowest deadline-miss rate and total UAV-side communication energy among the considered schemes. Compared with DE-UBAC, GRU-DEPPO reduces the deadline-miss rate by approximately 61% and inter-UAV energy imbalance by approximately 40%.

title: LLM Multi-Agent Systems Are Vulnerable to Herding and Runaway Cascades
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate in multi-agent systems where they collaborate by responding to others' choices, creating endogenous feedback loops with vulnerability to social influence, herding behavior and runaway cascades. Following the design of the classic Music Lab experiment, we tested this vulnerability in large populations of LLM agents that recommended unfamiliar songs, with or without exposure to cumulative recommendation counts. Exposure led to runaway cascades that generated extreme and unpredictable collective recommendations increasingly divergent from a song's intrinsic appeal. Compared to humans, LLM populations were generally far more susceptible to herding behavior, and unlike humans, LLM cascades were less able to self-correct. This vulnerability has implications for multi-agent collaboration in recommender systems, automated evaluation, complex problem-solving, and unauthorized conspiracies.

title: Axial Perturbations of Extended Tolman III in the New $f(R,T)$ Theory
abstract: We investigate compact objects using the extended Tolman III equation of state in the framework of $f(R,T)=R+2χT$ gravity. In the matter sector of the Lagrangian density, we employ a new formalism based on the evaluation of the second-order derivative of the matter Lagrangian with respect to the metric \cite{Jayawiguna:2026das}. We analyze the corresponding observational signatures through axial gravitational perturbations including stellar stability and gravitational echo. We find that the effective potential in $f(R,T)$ gravity is wider and deeper than its counterpart in general relativity (GR). The quasinormal-mode (QNM) frequencies are calculated using the Bohr--Sommerfeld (BS) fitting and both the lower- and higher-order Wentzel--Kramers--Brillouin (WKB) approximations. For the ultracompact configurations considered, trapped modes can tunnel through the potential barrier, giving rise to gravitational-wave echoes. The imaginary parts of the QNM frequencies are found to be negative, $\Im(ω_n M)<0$, indicating that the perturbations decay exponentially with time. Our results show that the echo train in GR contains more echoes than that in $f(R,T)$ gravity. Finally, assuming that the stellar object is a neutron star and adopting a stellar radius consistent with measurements by the Neutron Star Interior Composition Explorer (NICER), we find that the $f(R,T)$ gravity model yields a characteristic frequency consistent with the estimated frequency associated with GW170817 for $β= 4.663\times10^{-1}$ and $χ=0.96π$, whereas the corresponding GR model does not exhibit comparable agreement.

title: Quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball
abstract: In this paper, we study the quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball in hyperbolic space. We construct a locally constrained nonlinear curvature flow that preserves the $k$-th quermassintegral while monotonically increasing the $l$-th quermassintegral for any $(1\leq l<k\leq n)$. Using this flow, we establish a full family of the quermassintegral inequalities for horo-convex capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball with contact angle $θ\in(0,π/2]$. Moreover, we weaken the horo-convexity to convexity and obtain the quermassintegral inequalities for convex capillary hypersurfaces between the $n$-th and $l$-th quermassintegrals.

title: Lomb-Scargle Recovery of Periodic Binary Signals across Black Hole Mass and Cadence
abstract: Searches for periodic supermassive black hole binaries in quasar light curves rely on recovery fractions, the share of injected signals detected, which forecasts use as detection efficiencies. Lin, Charisi, & Haiman (2026) measured them for the Lomb-Scargle periodogram on damped-random-walk light curves matched to 12,400 bright, high-mass Palomar Transient Factory (PTF) quasars with Sloan Digital Sky Survey Data Release 7 (DR7) masses. To test them over four decades of mass, we inject their sinusoidal and sawtooth signals into light curves of mergers in the TNG100-1 cosmological simulation, with magnitudes drawn from DR7 quasars of similar mass (extrapolated at low mass). We apply their threshold in each frequency bin, set by $10^5$ noise-only light curves per binary, on observed PTF cadences, one Stripe 82 cadence and an LSST-like cadence (Legacy Survey of Space and Time). At fixed absolute magnitude $M_i=-23$, sinusoid recovery falls toward high mass, and with DR7 magnitudes it climbs above about $10^8\,M_\odot$, so the magnitude assignment sets the sign of the trend. Above $10^8\,M_\odot$, where their sample lies, PTF sinusoid recovery is 39.8 against their 44.7 per cent. At LSST-like cadence sinusoid recovery is 76.9 per cent, about three times their 22.6 per cent, for reasons mostly unidentified. Denser sampling of the same PTF baselines did not lower recovery in any test. Even at LSST-like cadence we miss most sawtooth signals above $10^8\,M_\odot$. We tabulate recovery per 0.5-dex mass bin and cadence, with low-mass values likely too high for a deeper survey.

title: A Chiral Nelson-Barr Relaxion
abstract: We present the chiral Nelson-Barr relaxion model, an extension of the Nelson-Barr relaxion framework with a gauged chiral $\mathrm{U}(1)$ symmetry. It includes vector-like quarks to cancel gauge anomalies and a scalar whose vacuum expectation value generates their masses. The chiral symmetry forbids the leading operators responsible for the Nelson-Barr and clockwork quality problems. Right-handed neutrinos generate light-neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism and permit thermal leptogenesis. For the particular coupling considered, relaxion phenomenology gives $f_{\mathrm{max}}^{\mathrm{pheno}}\sim 4\times 10^{11}\ \mathrm{GeV}$, about eight times the corresponding phenomenological ceiling in the original model. The model can accommodate thermal leptogenesis if its right-handed-neutrino masses and reheating history satisfy the required temperature bounds.

title: Evaluation of Front-End Feature Matching for Lunar Visual SLAM
abstract: Lunar rovers will primarily rely on cameras for localization until navigation satellite services are deployed, and will continue to need them afterwards for relative navigation, hazard detection, and surface operations. Visual odometry (VO) and Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) mostly estimate motion by matching features between frames. However, feature matchers are developed on urban, indoor and driving scenes, planetary studies compare them on orbital registration or within complete SLAM systems, and real lunar imagery with reference poses is scarce, so matching between rover frames on low-texture, harshly lit terrain, and its effect on VO, has not been compared. We benchmark eleven classical and learned detector-matcher combinations on nine synthetic, lunar-testbed, and terrestrial-analogue datasets, and a feature tracker, scoring pairwise pose accuracy against baseline and the trajectory error of the resulting VO. Under a common rotation-only metric, the SuperPoint pairings outperform SIFT with ratio-tested FLANN matching on both lunar testbeds and one analogue site, with smaller or unresolved differences on synthetic data. When rotation and translation direction are scored jointly, this SIFT pairing exceeds both SuperPoint pairings on four synthetic datasets, so synthetic results alone do not establish relative performance on real rover imagery. In stereo VO, the SuperPoint pairings are not consistently more accurate than SIFT, but only they keep tracking on all eight sequential datasets. Pairings with classical detectors depend on lighting while SuperPoint changes little: a low spotlight makes them more accurate than diffuse light on the same testbed views, consistent with more contrast and detected keypoints. SuperPoint with LightGlue is the fastest learned combination (16 ms per frame), and DINOv2 retrieval proposals still need geometric verification.

title: GWDM: A Guided Wavelet Diffusion Model for Realistic Histopathology Image Generation
abstract: Histopathology images are recognized as a reliable and comprehensive modality for Deep Learning (DL) based diagnosis. However, effectiveness is constrained by limited large-scale annotated datasets, as collecting expert-labeled medical data is costly and time-intensive. Recent advances in generative models, particularly diffusion models, demonstrate strong capabilities in synthesizing medically relevant content for dataset augmentation. Existing generative frameworks treat histopathology patches as generic natural images, failing to enforce biological constraints such as histomorphological structures and heterogeneous staining patterns essential for valid synthesis. We propose a guided wavelet diffusion model (GWDM) framework that captures image details at multiple scales using wavelets and leverages controllable conditioning based on domain-specific histopathological features (e.g., tissue patterns and color variations). We further formulate a histomorphological guidance loss applied to real and generated patches. A loss ramping strategy gradually introduces these constraints during training, ensuring stable optimization and robust modeling of tissue architecture. GWDM was evaluated on three benchmark datasets (BCSS, MoNuSeg, and PAIP2019), consistently outperforming state-of-the-art generative methods. Ablation studies confirmed that domain-guided conditioning, perceptual loss, and structural similarity loss each contribute meaningfully to synthesis quality. Downstream nuclei and tissue segmentation experiments further validated the clinical utility of GWDM-generated images, demonstrating consistent performance improvements when synthetic data augments real training sets. This work shows that domain-specific conditioning and dual-loss optimization generate realistic histopathology patches, reducing data scarcity and improving clinical downstream segmentation performance.

title: Report the tolerance, not the count: exact phylogenetic distance deconvolution with incomplete references
abstract: Phylogenetic distance deconvolution represents mixture-to-reference distances by weighted sources placed on a reference tree. We study the minimum number of strictly interior sources that explains a distance profile, and what incomplete references cost. On a positive-rational reduced tree we give an exact algorithm with 2^O(K) poly(B) bit complexity for a free positive mean pendant and any nonempty set of observed leaves. With arbitrary missing references and a prescribed pendant the problem is W[1]-hard in the source budget K, even on positive binary trees supplied with a strict explanation using at most K+1 sources. We then use the algorithm as an instrument. Removing references can only lower the minimum source count, never raise it. The direction is a theorem at every error tolerance and held without exception in 23,545 draws, so which references are missing matters more than how many. Two adversarially chosen references suffice, at the median, to destroy uniqueness of the minimum explanation, and that number does not grow with panel size (Spearman 0.203, p = 0.15, over 20 to 353 references) where random loss scales linearly. Discarding 7,931 of 10,575 references from a real 16S panel at random costs 1.8% of the tolerance at which one source suffices. Discarding comparably many as whole clades costs 90%. That tolerance needs neither ground truth nor an error model, which makes the model measurable on real data. Published distance estimates exceed it in 296 of 296 cases. The mixture inferred by the published heuristic reproduces real observations better than the configuration that generated them in 282 of 296. The phenomenon is not unobservable in practice. It is unobservable through a point estimate of the count. Methods for this problem should report the tolerance at which an explanation of a given size exists.

title: One Pretrained Decision Model Is Enough for Training-Free Generalist Graph Anomaly Detection
abstract: Graph anomaly detection (GAD) aims to identify irregular entities in graph-structured data, yet heterogeneous anomaly patterns and distributional differences across graphs challenge generalizable detection. Existing training-free approaches avoid task-specific optimization but primarily rely on predefined numerical scoring rules, leaving the semantic interpretation of heterogeneous anomaly evidence largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose Jev-GAD, a training-free generalist graph anomaly detection framework that bridges heterogeneous numerical evidence and pretrained decision mechanisms. To address heterogeneous anomaly patterns, we construct complementary structural, attribute, and neighborhood evidence and transform heterogeneous statistics into graph-relative anomaly percentiles. To move beyond predefined numerical scoring rules, we leverage a single frozen pretrained language model for evidence-conditioned anomaly assessment. To bridge the semantic gap between numerical evidence and pretrained models, we design a semantic Graph-to-State (G2S) transformation that organizes graph context and semantically labeled node evidence into structured decision states for non-generative option-logit readout. The resulting decision scores are integrated with four complementary statistical scores through equal-weight rank-based fusion, without GAD-specific gradient-based optimization. Extensive experiments on seven graph anomaly detection benchmarks spanning citation, social, and co-review networks demonstrate the effectiveness of Jev-GAD, achieving average AUROC and AUPRC scores of 89.18\% and 52.40\%, respectively. Further analyses validate the contributions of pretrained decision readout and semantic evidence grounding.

title: Where meanings converge and diverge: Revisiting linguistic relativity across 81 languages
abstract: Do people who speak different languages organize concepts in similar ways? This question lies at the heart of the Sapir--Whorf hypothesis and debates about linguistic relativity. Shared basic meanings, however, need not imply shared relations among them. We compared relations among 196 basic concepts across 81 languages, using word embeddings from two multilingual models to quantify conceptual structure expressed in language. Cross-language correspondence was greater for sociocultural meanings than for meanings concerning nature and motion, a contrast recurring across models and classifications. Within the sociocultural domain, relational differences increased with geographic separation; less closely related languages differed more across all domains. These findings suggest that universality and relativity are interwoven across conceptual domains. They inform an account in which shared cognitive resources interact with linguistic and local experience, and predict greater cross-language correspondence in human semantic judgments for sociocultural than for nature and motion meanings.

title: ProQuant: Preserving Expert Quality over Quantity in Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models reduce computation through sparse activation but still incur substantial storage costs. Mixed-precision post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces these costs by quantizing different model components at different bit widths, but existing methods often struggle to preserve generation quality under tight bit budgets. We identify two key challenges: (1) nonlinear quantization errors at extremely low precision are underestimated when cross-layer propagation is ignored; (2) direct router fine-tuning may cause routing drift, and calibration gains may not generalize to downstream tasks. To address these issues, we propose ProQuant, a weight-only PTQ framework for MoE models. Prune-or-Prioritize Mixed-Precision Allocation (PoP) jointly optimizes expert pruning and bit-width assignment. It allows higher-precision experts to substitute for severely degraded ones while improving bit-budget utilization. Routing-Consistent RMSNorm Finetune (RoCo) adapts expert input representations through mathematically equivalent transformations. It compensates for quantization errors to reduce routing drift. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ProQuant outperforms existing methods across diverse generative tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/ThrowBug/ProQuant.git.

title: ABRA: Agent-Bound UI for Human-Agent Communication beyond Chat with Reusable Views
abstract: Agents can create rich representations, yet these representations are rarely used as a medium for expressing user intent. We present Agent-Bound UI, an interaction model that separates reusable interaction structures from task-specific meanings. Agents bind task-specific meanings to interactions in reusable views and publish the resulting bindings as shared state, enabling humans and agents to understand and act on shared surfaces whose meanings vary across tasks. We implement ABRA, a framework-agnostic prototype of Agent-Bound UI, in which users and agents collaborate through chat and shared interactive canvases. We demonstrate ABRA through a representative use case and evaluate four LLM-backed agents on canvas authoring, owner-side consequence resolution, and cross-agent invocation. The code and demo video are available at https://github.com/megagonlabs/abra.

title: DeXplicit: Making Physical State Explicit in Dexterous Manipulation World Models
abstract: Before acting on an object, a robot needs to anticipate how its hand motion will change the physical world and what the resulting scene will look like. Existing approaches typically entangle action-conditioned dynamics, camera motion, and visual synthesis within a video generation model, or represent dynamics as point trajectories without explicit object structure. We introduce DeXplicit, a dexterous manipulation world model that instead predicts how the world evolves explicitly in metric 3D before rendering its visual consequences. Given an initial scene and a future hand trajectory, a lightweight 3D dynamics network predicts object-centric motion and deformation, providing structured and geometrically grounded future world states. These predictions then serve as a strong scaffold for video generation: appearance is transported through the predicted 3D motion and projected into future views, allowing the renderer to focus on completing uncertain and newly visible content rather than implicitly learning world dynamics from pixels. This explicit-3D-first decomposition also enables efficient causal generation, requiring only two denoising steps per block while conditioning on generated history. Across HOT3D, OakInk2, and PhysTwin, DeXplicit reduces moved-point error by 27-40% relative to PointWorld and improves object fidelity IoU+ by 47% on HOT3D under a shared renderer. Our design with two-step causal generation achieves a 57x speedup from our 14B bi-directional configuration in video synthesis.

title: Anomaly Score Preserving Data Poisoning Attacks on Data-Driven Controller Design
abstract: This paper investigates stealthy data poisoning attacks against data-driven controller synthesis and develops an attack generation method. During data collection, an attacker can sequentially manipulate state measurements, while the defender attempts to detect such manipulation using a residual-based anomaly score based on the Mahalanobis distance. Under suitable assumptions on the defender's prior knowledge, we characterize the class of time-varying affine transformations that preserve the anomaly score for arbitrary data and parameterize this class by the orthogonal group. Based on this characterization, we formulate attack design under the stealthiness condition as an optimization problem over the orthogonal group and propose a Riemannian gradient method. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed attack can degrade closed-loop performance while remaining stealthy.

title: MixJudge: Learning a Language-Queryable Critic for Vocal Mixing
abstract: Mixing requires not only applying processing but also assessing the resulting mix. Audio-language models can provide conversa- tional mixing advice, but existing evaluations do not separately test whether they can judge specific mixing issues. Since professional supervision for such judgments is scarce, we construct a curriculum of 11 vocal-mix issues at multiple severity levels and use it to train MixJudge, a language-queryable audio critic. MixJudge shows its ability to retrieve mixing issues, distinguish opposite issues, and order the severity of an issue. Moreover, its judgments transfer to menu selection: given a set of processing candidates, MixJudge often favors versions acoustically closer to a held-out professional version, demonstrating how explicit mixing judgment can support comparison and downstream mixing decisions.

title: Constraints on interacting dark energy with a constant equation of state in light of DESI DR2: The role of the interaction term
abstract: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) analyses suggest a preference for an evolving dark energy equation of state (EoS) that crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Interactions between dark energy and dark matter can also produce an apparent phantom-divide crossing in the effective dark energy EoS. In this work, we investigate interacting dark energy (IDE) models with a constant EoS parameter $w$, using cosmic microwave background (CMB) observations from Planck, ACT, and SPT, DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and type Ia supernova data from PantheonPlus, DES-Dovekie, and DESY5. We consider four typical forms of the interaction term $Q$. Our results show that the IDE models with $Q\proptoρ_{\rm de}$ generally exhibit a stronger preference for nonzero dark-sector interactions. In particular, for the CMB+DESI+DES-Dovekie data, the IDE model with $Q=βH_0ρ_{\rm de}$ yields $β=-2.52^{+0.80}_{-0.54}$ and $w=-1.510^{+0.170}_{-0.120}$, corresponding to deviations from $β=0$ and $w=-1$ at the $3.2σ$ and $3.0σ$ levels, respectively. Interestingly, the effective EoS of the IDE model with $Q=βH_0ρ_{\rm de}$ exhibits a redshift evolution resembling that of the $w_0w_a$CDM model, crossing the phantom divide. Bayesian evidence further indicates that this IDE model is favored over $Λ$CDM and the other three IDE models. Our analysis helps identify which interaction forms better account for current cosmological observations.

title: Invisibilization as a Source of Probability Bias in Language Models
abstract: Language models are aligned to avoid using protected attributes such as race, ethnicity, and gender to inform their responses. Therefore, they increasingly refuse or hedge when such attributes appear in a prompt. However, if a system must decide how much to learn from what people tell it, it is costly to refuse valuable information because of its source. In this article, we measure the cost of declining information in a two-urn game with an exact Bayesian answer. We present leading LLM models from two developers (OpenAI and Anthropic) with a prompt that requires them to decide how far to trust an unverifiable report from a participant whose description we randomize across ten configurations (6,600 sessions). We show that leading models often decline to assess the reporter, treating information as worthless at rates set by the description rather than by the evidence. At its widest, models decline a Black-described reporter 46% of the time and a white-described reporter 9%; yet, when they do assess the information, the Black-described reporter receives slightly more trust. The bias is invisible to audits that compare average trust or look only at assessed cases. It grows with reasoning effort, follows words rather than categories (models invoke race for "Black" but not for its Spanish translation negro, and never for "Indigenous"), and worsens under warning instructions a practitioner would try first. We also present a scoring option that reduces the refusal rate bias. When a model's trust is scored against revealed truth over repeated rounds, it credits identical records equally. In four of five configurations from Anthropic and OpenAI, the racial gap in trust falls below 0.02 by the last rounds.

title: EBV-CAN: Vision--Language Grounding for Contact-Aided Endoscope Navigation
abstract: Flexible endoscopes exploit structural compliance to traverse narrow lumens, pipes, and cavities, where navigation involves distributed environmental contact. This compliance makes tip motion depend on the evolving support configuration. We present external bird's-eye-view contact-aided navigation (EBV-CAN), a vision-language policy that combines one initial global static bird's-eye image with evolving endoscopic observations and motor state. Three supervised semantic queries locate the tip, next waypoint, and instructed target on the cached global image; their residual representations predict bending and insertion commands. We introduce the Vision-Language Contact-Aided (VLCA) dataset, linking 517 demonstrations and 75k action samples to 958k spatial entries and 93k remaining-route records. On 50 held-out episodes, tip-coordinate and waypoint localization reach 97.5% and 94.8%. Swapping the target instruction under identical observations changes target attention and motor output across 17 dual-target episodes. Across 1,920 physical trials of eight policies trained under a shared protocol, EBV-CAN achieves 183/240 successes (76.25%) under automatic blue-area scoring. Gated recurrent unit behavior cloning (GRU-BC) achieves the lowest matched-task offline mean absolute error (MAE), 0.056, and 1/240 physical successes, establishing distinct rankings for action imitation and task completion. Successful multi-guide executions and representative failures connect spatial progress, steering transitions, and visibility to physical navigation.

title: Schatten limits for semi-commutators in Toeplitz quantization on Fock space
abstract: We solve a problem posed by Hu and Virtanen by characterizing, for every $0<p<\infty$, the bounded symbols $f$ for which $T_f^{(t)}T_g^{(t)}-T_{fg}^{(t)}$ tends to zero in the unnormalized Schatten $p$-norm or quasi-norm as $t\to0^+$ for every fixed bounded $g$. The setting is weighted Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^n$ with weights whose real Hessians are uniformly positive and bounded. Only constants satisfy the limit when $p<2n$; at $p=2n$, it is equivalent to the weak real gradient belonging to $L^{2n}(\mathbb R^{2n})$. When $p>2n$, the limit is characterized by relative weak compactness in $L^1(\mathbb R^{2n})$ of normalized local mean oscillation densities. For $p\ge2$, uniform convergence over $\|g\|_\infty\le1$ is equivalent to vanishing density mass. A continuous compactly supported counterexample for $p>2n$ shows that bounded density mass and convergence for $g=\bar f$ do not imply convergence for every fixed bounded $g$. The symbol classes are weight-independent unital algebras, yielding limits for finite Toeplitz products and commutators; quantitative Hölder estimates also give finite-rank approximation bounds. The Gaussian case transfers to anti-Wick quantization by unitary equivalence. On compact Kähler manifolds with positive line bundles, we prove a Hölder sufficient condition, including the endpoint, for each fixed bounded second symbol. A projective-line example shows that trace norm convergence can fail for a smooth first symbol and a fixed bounded second symbol. The proofs combine local holomorphic approximation, Schatten and Sobolev estimates, singular integral methods, and the Dunford--Pettis criterion.

title: Hasegawa-Mima equation as limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system
abstract: We prove that the Hasegawa-Mima equation (HME) is the limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system in a special scaling regime. The proof relies on the derivation of a uniform estimate independent of the scaling parameter, using the particular structure of the singular system and the identification of a combination of the unknowns that compensates for fast oscillations in time. We also show that HME allow us to investigate a conditional property of inverse energy cascade and drift waves.

title: An Introduction to World Models for Generalist Agents
abstract: World models have recently emerged as a promising direction toward developing generalist agents capable of understanding, predicting, and interacting with diverse environments. However, despite growing interest, the concept of a world model remains loosely defined, encompassing approaches ranging from predictive dynamics models and learned simulators to models that jointly generate future observations and actions. This introductory paper aims to clarify the concept of world models and provide a unified perspective on their role in developing generalist agents. Starting from the partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) framework, we connect world modeling to classical control, dynamical systems, signal processing, and reinforcement learning. We introduce different approaches to world modeling, emphasizing the knowledge they capture, their learning objectives, and how they support decision-making. We further explore the relationship between world modeling and policy learning, highlighting how these capabilities can be unified through conditional prediction without requiring separate models. Rather than offering an exhaustive survey of existing methods, this paper focuses on fundamental concepts, modeling principles, and connections, with the goal of providing an accessible and unified introduction to world models for generalist agents.

title: Agentic Knowledge-Model Co-Evolution via Consistency Regularization
abstract: LLM agents can evolve by learning from accumulated experience. Existing approaches extract reusable external knowledge, such as skills and memories, from experience to guide subsequent task solving, with some further internalizing this knowledge through model training. However, different ways of analyzing and transforming the same experience can yield knowledge with substantially different utility, even when the resulting guidance appears reasonable. Inspired by consistency regularization, we identify consistent utility gains across different ways of analyzing the same experience, rather than relying on any single way of analyzing it. We introduce SPLICE, a framework for consistency-regularized knowledge-model co-evolution. It constructs evolution views by perturbing how the same experience is analyzed, producing different knowledge candidates. Knowledge updates are then guided by common gain, which accounts for utility gains and their consistency across views. During model evolution, self-distillation internalizes the evolved knowledge alongside reinforcement learning, using knowledge associated with consistent utility degradation as a contrastive reference. The two processes interleave, with model updates driving further knowledge evolution. Experiments across diverse domains show that SPLICE outperforms knowledge evolution and model training baselines by up to 7.1 and 4.6 points in average accuracy, while its evolved knowledge reduces output tokens per correct solution by up to 44% and transfers across model sizes and families.

title: Gandalf: Flash Shall Not Die! Increasing Flash Storage Lifetime for KV Cache Offloading in LLM Serving
abstract: KV caching reduces the serving cost of large language models (LLMs), but the growing KV cache footprint is increasingly exceeds GPU and host-memory capacity. Therefore, people use SSD to expand the KV cache storage capacity with high I/O bandwidth. However, in production LLM workload, such as multi-round conversation and LLM agents, the total amount of KV cache writes significantly exceeds SSD capacity, shortening SSD lifetime from years to months. To improve SSD lifetime, a natural solution is to reduce the KV cache writes by gating the KV cache writes via historical access patterns. However, that significantly lowers the KV cache hit rate (and increase the LLM serving cost) since KV caches from different attention types might have identical historical access pattern but different future access patterns. Our insight is that, to reduce KV cache writes without hurting KV cache hit rate, one need to not only consider the access pattern, but also application-level information such as the attention type of KV cache. Leveraging this observation, we propose Gandalf , the first SSD KV cache offloading system with SSD life time awareness. Gandalf prioritize the admission of full-attention KV cache into SSD over the cache generated by other types of attention, which significantly increases SSD lifetime without sacrificing cache hit rate. Our evaluation shows that Gandalf extends the SSD lifetime by 7.3X on average, while having negligible impact on cache hit rate across multiple workload traces and wide range of hardware capacity. Gandalf design can be extended to other flash-based storage, such as High Bandwidth Flash (HBF).

title: Trace2World: Reconstructing App Worlds from Real Interaction Traces for Scalable GUI Agent Training
abstract: Scaling GUI reinforcement learning requires environments that preserve real-app behavior. Yet coupling behavior inference with coding can turn partial traces into runnable mocks with incorrect state transitions. We introduce \textbf{Trace2World}, which separates global behavior reconstruction from implementation. It reconciles traces into a shared, source-linked app model, then compiles an executable environment. Independent replay of source workflows localizes mismatches for bounded implementation repair. Validated worlds then support learner-adaptive task and environment augmentation within source-supported behavior. From 1,570 traces, Trace2World constructs 50 environments. On 200 workflows across ten apps, 91.1% are reproduced end to end, versus 59.8% for the strongest matched task-local baseline. Source-grounded validation retains 94.0% of simulated training gains on real devices, versus 54.7% under self-validation. Learner guidance raises benchmark success from 56.9% to 61.1%. Training in Trace2World further improves the model by 20.2 points on our benchmark, 5.4--16.2 points across four external GUI benchmarks, and 16.3 points on 100 real-device tasks. Reliable reconstruction separates what behavior source evidence supports from whether the implementation preserves it.

title: Advancing oxygen-enhanced MRI acquisition and modelling through dynamic $ΔR_{1}$ and $ΔR_2^*$ sensing
abstract: Purpose: To develop a multiparametric mapping framework for quantifying fat- and water-specific longitudinal and effective transverse relaxation rates, as well as changes in these parameters induced by a gas challenge. Theory and Methods: The proposed framework, termed SR-Fat DESPOT (single-reference fat-water separated driven equilibrium single-pulse observation of $T_1$), combines a two-component signal model with a single-reference variable flip angle (SR-VFA) approach. The signal model explicitly incorporates gas challenge-induced changes in relaxation rates. The single-reference acquisition strategy reduces data acquisition requirements while preserving sensitivity to both baseline parameters and dynamic changes. Sequence parameters were optimized using Cramer-Rao lower bound theory. SR-Fat DESPOT was evaluated using a modified open-surce abdominal numerical phantom and in two in vivo experiments: a single participant test-retest experiment and a pilot study with six participants. Results: In the abdominal numerical phantom, SR-Fat DESPOT was accurate for quantification of baseline relaxation rates with a normalized median absolute error (nMedAE) <3% for signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) >30 when comparing ground truth and estimates. SR-Fat DESPOT was also able to accurately recover median changes in relaxation rates, with differences within 0.001 $s^-1$ when compared to ground truth. In vivo, SR-Fat DESPOT measured changes in relaxation rates for spleen, kidneys, liver, and muscle under 100% O2 breathing, consistent with reports in literature. Changes detected in the spleen and kidneys were statistically significant across participants. Conclusion: SR-Fat DESPOT can quantify changes in relaxation rates induced by a gas challenge while reducing data requirements compared to more conventional approaches used in MR-oximetry literature.

title: VLTest: Finding Joint Image-Text Failures in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly embedded in software systems. Testing them raises two problems. Mutating either input can change the expected answer, so an output change is not by itself a failure. Some failures appear only when both inputs are mutated; attributing them to the combination requires testing each mutation alone. We present VLTest, a black-box VLM testing approach. It generates image variants by editing VQGAN latent codes and text variants with a rewrite-expand-prune pipeline, filters variants likely to change the expected answer, and tests each variant alone before testing combinations, so every joint failure has four matched cells. A VLM judge confirms a failure only after checking that the input keeps the expected answer. On three tasks with eight VLMs, including two commercial API models, the oracle confirms 81.7% of the candidates, with 88.8% to 94.6% precision against human labels, and four-cell confirmation rejects 22.5% of joint candidates. Under the same budget, VLTest's generators find 1.8 to 2.5 times as many confirmed failures as SINVAD and TextFooler, and its joint tests find 91 to 197 attributed joint failures per 1,000 joint calls, 1.3 times as many as the same pairing applied to the baselines' variants.

title: A Modified Direct Eigenvalue Swapping Algorithm with Guaranteed Stability
abstract: For a given matrix \( A \) in the real Schur form, the eigenvalue swapping algorithm is used to swap two adjacent diagonal blocks. In LAPACK, this operation is performed by the subroutine~\texttt{SLAEXC}/\texttt{DLAEXC}, which is based on a direct swapping algorithm proposed by Bai and Demmel in 1993. In this work, we present a thorough error analysis of a modified direct swapping algorithm. By a carefully designed pivoted Givens QR factorization, this algorithm can achieve an error bound of the form \( O( \boldsymbol{u} \lVert A \rVert ) \) under mild assumptions, where \( \boldsymbol{u} \) is the unit roundoff. We present empirical evidence to illustrate the superior stability of our algorithm over existing approaches.

title: GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL
abstract: Training large language models for complex reasoning tasks relies on two complementary signals: sparse, outcome-grounded reinforcement learning (RL) for correctness, and dense, token-level distillation for guidance. However, complementarity in supervision does not guarantee compatibility in optimization; imitation-focused distillation can conflict with the outcome-driven RL objective, and existing hybrids lack a principled resolution. We propose \textbf{GIFT} (\textbf{G}radient-\textbf{I}nformed \textbf{F}il\textbf{T}ering for Distillation-Augmented Reasoning RL), a novel method that directly addresses the allocation problem of which teacher updates to apply. GIFT performs a token-level geometric analysis, decomposing the distillation gradient into a component \textbf{parallel} to the RL gradient, which measures first-order conflict and provides a \textbf{safety} filter, and a component \textbf{orthogonal} to it, which quantifies novel directional guidance and provides a measure of \textbf{value}. This decomposition yields a principled scoring rule to rank token-level guidance. We combine this with a progressive \textbf{coverage annealing} schedule that shrinks the budget of tokens receiving distillation, ensuring that the most conflicting updates are discarded first while the most complementary ones are retained at full strength. This facilitates a smooth transition from dense, geometrically-filtered guidance to a pure, outcome-grounded objective at convergence. Extensive experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks show that GIFT consistently outperforms strong baselines across multiple model scales, achieving relative gains of up to 9.5\% on difficult mathematical reasoning tasks. Code: https://github.com/lilifree/GIFT

title: OpenAI partially disproves Littlewood's 1961 $L^α$-flat theorem
abstract: We present a counterexample, produced by OpenAI, to Littlewood's 1961 theorem on $L^α$-flat polynomials. The theorem asserts that no $L^α$-flat polynomials exist within the class of trigonometric polynomials of the form$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m \cos(mθ+α_m), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}^*,$$satisfying$$k\, n^2 \sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m^2 \;\leq\; \sum_{m=1}^{n} m^2 a_m^2,$$where $k$ is an absolute constant (alternatively expressed on the right-hand side as $K = 1/k$). We show that OpenAI's counterexample is contained within the class of hyper-lacunary sequences. Consequently, it offers only a limited refutation, as such sequences fail to satisfy an implicit assumption of Littlewood's theorem. We also discuss broader questions surrounding this counterexample and provide a brief historical overview.

title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high inference efficiency using optimized GPU kernels generated by just-in-time (JIT) compilation frameworks such as Triton. Triton compiles GPU kernels through an MLIR/LLVM-based pipeline. We investigate whether a Rowhammer-induced bit-flip in the CPU's DRAM can degrade GPU-based LLM inference performance while preserving output correctness. We present LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack that causes LLM inference slowdown by inducing a bit-flip in Triton's compilation pipeline. A bit-flip in a performance-critical optimization pass causes Triton to generate a functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernel. Since Triton caches the generated kernel on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent slowdown across subsequent inference executions. Triton's target-independent stages are shared across GPU vendors, which makes our attack GPU vendor-agnostic. To identify exploitable bit-flip locations without manual inspection, we build Karnage, a tool that isolates useful bit-flip locations in Triton's target-independent compilation pipeline. We evaluate LLVMHammer across a diverse set of LLMs, including Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and Deepseek-llm-7B-chat, across NVIDIA RTX 4090 and AMD RX 7900 XTX GPUs. LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16\%, which, in turn, can translate into additional annual operating costs at the scale of multi-GPU deployments. We further show that LLVMhammer can also corrupt LLM outputs across different GPU vendors, reducing BERTScore to as low as 25\%, illustrating the broader security implications of bit-flips in Triton's compilation pipeline.

title: WovenAnchor Matcher: Specialized Intra- and Inter-Image Context Modeling for Feature Matching
abstract: Semi-dense local feature matching commonly aggregates contextual information before coarse-to-fine correspondence estimation. However, intra-image and inter-image aggregation serve different roles: the former should propagate spatial evidence within each image while retaining structured two-dimensional dependencies, whereas the latter should gather information from plausible corresponding regions while limiting noise from unrelated locations. We propose WovenAnchor Matcher (WAM), a semi-dense matching framework based on role-specialized context aggregation. WAM introduces two complementary operators. WovenMamba performs intra-image aggregation through horizontal-then-vertical state-space propagation, allowing vertical updates to operate on horizontally contextualized features and thereby encouraging a structured two-dimensional receptive-field bias. AnchorCrossAttention performs inter-image aggregation by using cross-attention to gather context from plausible corresponding regions across the image pair. It performs this exchange over local representative anchors that aggregate feature evidence within each window. On MegaDepth, WAM achieves 66.1 pose AUC@5$^\circ$, improving on the JamMa baseline by 2.0 AUC points under the same evaluation setup. Ablations show that removing or replacing either specialized component reduces accuracy, providing evidence that intra-image propagation and inter-image retrieval benefit from role-specific aggregation designs. Code and pretrained weights are available at https://github.com/mmaiLab/WovenAnchorMatcher.

title: When are metrizable linear subspaces of topological vector spaces finite-dimensional?
abstract: We study conditions that imply finite-dimensionality of metrizable or Frechet-Urysohn linear subspaces of topological vector spaces (TVS). We consider the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ of TVS: a space $L$ belongs to $\mathscr{D}_M$ (respectively, $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$) if every metrizable (respectively, Frechet-Urysohn) linear subspace of $L$ is finite-dimensional. Although the classes of metrizable spaces and of Frechet-Urysohn spaces differ substantially, the classes $\mathscr{D}_M$ and $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ are much closer to each other: in the Hrusak-Ramos-Garcia model, in which Malykhin's problem is solved, $\mathscr{D}_M=\mathscr{D}_{FU}$, whereas under MA+not CH, as shown in the paper, $\mathscr{D}_M\neq\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. For a locally convex space (LCS) $L$ we denote by $L_w$ the space $L$ with its weak topology and by $L'_{w^*}$ the dual space with the weak$^*$ topology. This paper investigates which LCS $L$ have the property that $L_w$ and $L'_{w^*}$ belong to $\mathscr{D}_M$ or $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$. Although the classes are close, different methods are used to study them: topological-algebraic ones for $\mathscr{D}_M$ (a criterion is obtained) and methods of measure theory and probability for $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$ (a sufficient condition is obtained). We prove that if an LCS $L$ admits a continuous norm, then $L_w\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; in particular, if $L$ admits a continuous norm and $L_w$ is Frechet-Urysohn, then $L$ is finite-dimensional. If the topology of an LCS $L$ is coarser than the topology induced by some complete norm on $L$ (for example, if $L$ is Banach), then $L'_{w^*}\in\mathscr{D}_{FU}$; completeness of the norm is essential here. The methods also apply to spaces of real-analytic functions and to the space of polynomials with the topology of pointwise convergence: these also belong to $\mathscr{D}_{FU}$.

title: A Computationally Efficient and Rate-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial Linear MDPs with (Aggregate) Bandit Feedback
abstract: We study episodic linear Markov decision processes with unknown transitions, adversarial losses, and bandit feedback. The state-of-the-art result for this setting (Liu et al., 2024) either achieves $\sqrt{K}$ regret with a computationally inefficient algorithm or achieves suboptimal $K^{3/4}$ regret, where $K$ is the number of episodes. Our work gives the first $\sqrt{K}$ regret with a polynomial-time algorithm. Our method reduces adversarial linear MDPs to adversarial linear bandits whose action set consists of policies' expected feature vectors. The central challenge is that this action set is unknown and can be estimated only through exploration. We address this challenge by constructing an approximate separation oracle for the action set that either generates executable policies from queried features, or refines an outer approximation of the action set. This approach draws inspiration from the reduction of van Erven et al. (2025) for linear contextual bandits and the oracle-efficient linear bandit algorithm of Ito et al. (2019), but additionally deals with the imprecision of the oracle. The resulting algorithm requires only aggregate loss feedback, and to our knowledge. This is the first polynomial-time algorithm for adversarial MDPs with aggregate feedback beyond the tabular case.

title: Is spectral predictability enough? Testing Ω-matching for synthetic pretraining under distribution shift
abstract: Synthetic pretraining under distribution shift requires deciding what synthetic data to use. A natural criterion is to match the spectral predictability $Ω$ of the source to the target, but is $Ω$ sufficient? We test this hypothesis, which we call predictability-aware pretraining, across three architectures (LSTM, PatchTST, TCN) and three seeds. Under ideal synthetic-to-synthetic conditions, $Ω$-matched pretraining can outperform even an oracle baseline (+46.8% MSE reduction, LSTM), though the benefit is already architecture-dependent. On the real-world ETTm1 benchmark, however, this relationship does not hold: sine-plus-noise pretraining at matched $Ω$ yields only a marginal mean improvement +2.3% averaged over all three architectures, up to +65.5% on individual channels), whereas $Ω$ matched chaotic ODE trajectories systematically degrade performance -13.2%). The two sources agree on the direction of transfer for only 53% of configurations across all three architectures (Pearson r=-0.02), indicating that $Ω$ carries little information about which source will transfer beneficially. We further observe an architecture-dependent asymmetry in the response to the direction of the $Ω$ gap. We conclude that $Ω$ matching can help in controlled settings but is not sufficient to predict transfer across sources, and we discuss additional signal properties that a source-selection criterion may need to consider.

title: What Lies Beyond Perception: A Partition Theory of the Limits of AI Evaluation and Oversight
abstract: Replacing the judge can move a benchmark score, and models can be trained to hide capabilities. Both put the evaluator in question: what can it certify? We develop a partition theory of evaluation from one principle: judgement is bounded by perception. An agent's discrimination is the partition of its inputs into classes it cannot tell apart. Discrimination is necessary for capability but not sufficient, so bounds on it bear directly on whether evaluation can show that a model lacks an ability. We prove a one-sided bound. An examinee whose partition refines its evaluator's has the discrimination to pass every test the evaluator can grade, provided each input has an acceptable reply. We define the echo test, which accepts any reply the evaluator perceives as identical to the input, and show that it is complete for the tests the evaluator can grade. Passing therefore certifies at most a floor on discrimination, never a ceiling, and only a sharper evaluator can raise it. Used to detect concealment, echo-test failure points the wrong way: under exhaustive probing it flags every honestly weaker examinee and no concealer that presents as the evaluator's peer. Exact imitation of a weaker model is undetectable by any behavioural evaluator. We extend the bound to ensembles of monitors and to channels a model controls, explain published findings on judge disagreement and sandbagging, and derive testable predictions. A safety case that argues from behavioural evaluation alone that a model lacks an ability must assume the model's cooperation.

title: Numerical Solution of Large-Scale Low-Rank Coupled Generalized Sylvester Equations
abstract: This paper develops projection methods for computing low-rank solutions to large-scale coupled generalized Sylvester equations. The dominant subspaces of these solutions are shown to be spanned by specific resolvent directions, motivating a Petrov--Galerkin projection framework. Conditions for the unique solvability of the projected coupled generalized Sylvester equations are also discussed. Based on these dominant subspaces, two algorithms are proposed: an extended Krylov-based projection algorithm and a rational Krylov-based projection algorithm. The former uses fixed shifts, whereas the latter uses adaptive shifts. Numerical experiments on large-scale benchmark problems demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve high accuracy and fast convergence.

title: Distinct stellar-parameter dependencies of granulation and mesogranulation in red giants
abstract: Granulation and mesogranulation represent different spatial and temporal scales of convection, but are commonly assumed to follow the same stellar atmospheric scaling relations in red giants. We test this assumption using the largest sample assembled for this purpose to date -- 9,328 Kepler red giants spanning the red giant branch and red clump phase, cross-matched with APOGEE stellar parameters. We model each star's power spectrum background to obtain the radius-corrected amplitude and characteristic frequency of both components, and derive empirical scaling relations with effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity through Bayesian model comparison. Gaussian Process and symbolic regression provide independent validation. We find that granulation and mesogranulation are not self-similar: their surface-gravity dependencies are statistically indistinguishable, consistent with a shared envelope geometry, but their temperature dependencies diverge: mesogranulation's amplitude rises steeply with Teff, whereas granulation's shows no statistically justified dependence, and both frequencies respond weakly and similarly. We propose that this pattern is consistent with granulation forming in a thin near-surface layer, where radiation takes over from convection and the Mach number depends only weakly on Teff. Mesogranulation originates deeper, where convection carries the full flux and its Mach number and cell size increase with Teff. Metallicity raises both amplitudes but has little effect on the frequencies. Our results indicate that the self-similarity assumption underlying two-component background models does not hold, with direct implications for background modeling and its downstream application in Galactic archaeology.

title: Astrometric detection of rocky exoplanets from inexpensive space platforms
abstract: The detection of orbiting exoplanets by way of astrometric monitoring of the host star to reveal gravitationally induced reflex motion requires extreme precision and measurement stability when targeting Earth-mass objects. Despite this, astrometry is widely regarded as the most promising avenue for the most desired of all targets: true Earth analogue systems in the solar neighbourhood. Formerly thought to require flagship class investment, recently several smaller concepts such as the TOLIMAN and SHERA missions have shown that detections are possible, at least in principle, from more modest space platforms. A key enabling feature is that these missions exploit narrow-angle astrometry. Observing only multiple star systems where the target provides its own astrometric reference greatly alleviates the challenges confronted by traditional astrometry with its reliance on distant, faint field stars. This principle underlies the TOLIMAN mission, for which progress and status is reported. However, only a tiny handful of nearby star systems are suited to such a TOLIMAN-like architecture. This paper discusses speculative optical concepts featuring ultra-stable telescopes of modest (<0.5m) aperture designed for astrometric monitoring of isolated single stars at the micro-arcsecond scales required for the discovery of Earth mass objects orbiting sun-like stars in temperate orbits. In simulation, highly sought-after neighbourhood systems such as Epsilon Eridani and Tau Ceti can be exhaustively searched for rocky planets with dedicated observing campaigns spanning several years, all from relatively inexpensive orbital platforms.

title: A Weakly Group Strategy-Proof and Pareto-Stable Matching Mechanism with Two-Sided Indifferences under Gross Substitutes
abstract: We study finite many-to-one matching markets with indifferences on both sides and publicly known firm preferences over sets of workers. A standard approach breaks ties uniformly at random and runs deferred acceptance, which is strategy-proof for workers but may select a weakly stable matching that is Pareto dominated under the agents' original preferences. For the broad class of markets in which each firm's preferences admit a gross substitutes (GS) representation, we construct a deterministic generalized deferred acceptance mechanism that is weakly stable, Pareto efficient with respect to both sides, worker weakly group strategy-proof, and implementable in strongly polynomial time given value oracles for the GS representations. This domain includes nonresponsive firm preferences, such as additive scores under matroid constraints and assignment values. Our analysis bridges ordinal matching with indifferences and competitive equilibria under imperfectly transferable utility. Although the mechanism uses only ordinal comparisons, it returns a seller-optimal equilibrium matching of a tiered auxiliary market, and the equilibrium structure of this market yields the stability, efficiency, and incentive guarantees.

title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.

title: An integer determinant approach to the length of Type II codes and the weights of shadows
abstract: It is well known that the length $n$ of a binary Type II code is divisible by $8$. The classical proof relies on Gleason's theorem on weight enumerators. Motivated by a question of Vera Pless, we give elementary proofs of this fact that avoid invariant theory. Our main tool is a congruence modulo $8$ for the determinant of the integer Gram matrix $AA^{\mathsf T}$ of a binary orthogonal matrix $A$, obtained directly from the Leibniz expansion. It gives a short proof of a theorem of Janusz: the number of rows of weight congruent to $3 \pmod 4$ in a binary orthogonal matrix is divisible by $4$. From this single statement we derive both the length restriction for Type II codes and the theorem of Conway and Sloane that every vector in the shadow of a binary self-dual code of length $n$ has weight congruent to $n/2 \pmod 4$. We also give two short character-theoretic proofs of the length restriction and explain how all of these arguments detect the Arf invariant of a quadratic form.

title: Adaptive Aerial Loco-Manipulation Policy Learning via LLM-Assisted Proactive Task Generation
abstract: Loco-manipulation extends the workspace of conventional manipulation by combining mobility with physical interaction, while aerial loco-manipulation further expands this capability into three-dimensional space, enabling robots to reach environments inaccessible to ground-based systems.
