abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) in Flying Networks (FNs) increasingly require mechanisms to translate high-level natural language objectives into executable missions. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated the feasibility of language-driven UAV control, existing approaches typically rely on static model configurations and overlook mission-aware performance variability. This paper presents AERIAL, a benchmark-driven framework for adaptive LLM selection in hybrid edge-cloud UAV control. AERIAL separates systematic model benchmarking from mission execution, deriving empirical scenario-model mappings and applying them at runtime for mission-aware selection. Evaluation across 720 automated simulation runs spanning navigation, spatial reasoning, and algorithm invocation revealed significant performance variability depending on scenario-model pairing. A case study integrating AERIAL with a FNs placement algorithm further validated the framework's ability to interface with domain-specific optimization modules through natural language. These results validate the effectiveness of AERIAL's adaptive model selection in improving reliability and operational robustness for autonomous UAV control in FNs.

title: What Does AI Success Look Like? A Mixed-Methods Analysis of Supranational AI Governance Instruments
abstract: In the last decade and in particular since 2018, supranational institutions have published policies, guidelines, and most recently regulations to govern development and use of Artificial Intelligence (AI). This paper aims to investigate the themes and dimensions of ``AI success'' set forth by instruments of AI governance issued by supranational bodies. To this end, we use a mixed-methods approach, combining manual thematic analysis and automated topic modelling approaches, to analyse a curated corpus of 13 documents issued by supranational bodies, including the European Union bodies, OECD, G20, UNESCO, United Nations, and the Council of Europe between 2018-2025. Based on the analysis and through the lens of sociology of expectations, we propose a novel categorisation scheme for AI success themes emerging from supranational bodies' documents. Drawing on the findings, we advance a set of policy recommendations, setting forward the need to move beyond high-level principles toward more coordinated approaches to AI governance.

title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+δ^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

title: Parameter Constraints on $f(R^{1+ε},T_{μν}T^{μν})$ Gravity from Exotic Compact Objects
abstract: According to General Relativity (GR), gravity is described as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy. Although GR has been highly successful in describing gravitational phenomena, exotic compact objects with high mass and strong gravitational fields, as well as low-mass objects, have motivated the study of modified theories of gravity. One of the modified gravity frameworks is $f(R,T^2) = R^{1 + ε} + ακ^2 T_{μν} T^{μν}$, which provides an extension of GR by introducing modifications to both the geometric and matter sectors. In this study, we investigate the mass-radius structure, physical viability, and stability of quark stars in $f(R,T^2)$ gravity using the MIT Bag Model equation of state. We compare results from the exact $f(R,T^2)$ model, its first-order Taylor expansion, and GR. The values of the gravity parameter $ε$ and $α$ are constrained by evaluating the ability of the model to reproduce the observed mass-radius configurations of compact objects, including HESS J1731-347 with a mass of $M = 0.77_{-0.17}^{+0.20} \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 10.4_{-0.78}^{+0.86}$ km, GW190814 with a mass of $M = 2.6 \, M_{\odot}$, PSR J1614-2230, with a mass of $M = 1.928 \pm 0.017 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R > 10$ km, and PSR J0437-4715, with a mass of $M = 1.418 \pm 0.037 \, M_{\odot}$ and a radius of $R = 11.36_{-0.63}^{+0.95}$ km. We assess the physical viability and stability of the stellar configurations using the energy conditions (strong, weak, null, and dominant) and the speed of sound. Overall, the $f(R,T^2)$ gravity model can accommodate quark star configurations and reproduce the observed properties of massive compact objects, particularly those associated with GW190814 and the lightest compact object observed, HESS J1731-347, respectively.

title: Dirac Structures and Reduction of Optimal Control Problems with Symmetries
abstract: We study the symmetry reduction of optimal control problems using Dirac structures. The first-order conditions of the Pontryagin Maximum Principle are written as an implicit Dirac system on the Pontryagin bundle. For a problem invariant under a Lie group, we reduce both the Lagrange-Pontryagin variational principle and the underlying Dirac structure, and prove that they yield the same reduced equations, which we identify with the Hamiltonian equations on the dual of the Atiyah algebroid. Reconstruction, independence of the principal connection, and the relation between criticality and optimality complete the picture. Dropping regularity, we give the Gotay-Nester-Hinds constraint algorithm a Dirac-geometric form and prove that symmetry reduction commutes with it. For control-linear systems whose admissible directions are horizontal for a principal connection, abnormal extremals lie on the leaf where the base costate vanishes, and the first secondary constraint is the degeneracy of the curvature pairing. We also give a reduced criterion for strict abnormality and a metric-free index form. Examples: a spacecraft with rotors (flat connection), the Heisenberg group (nowhere-zero curvature) and the Martinet problem (curvature vanishing on a hypersurface).

title: CANNBot-CAKE: Collaborative Agentic Kernel Evolution for Ascend NPU
abstract: Efficient custom operators are essential for modern deep learning workloads, yet developing high-performance kernels for Ascend NPUs remains slow, expert-intensive, and difficult to automate. Although AI agents now approach expert performance on GPU kernel benchmarks, current models remain less capable of generating AscendC kernels for NPUs, potentially reflecting the relative scarcity of relevant training data. We thus present CAKE, a CANN-native system for deployable custom operators that combines adaptive multi-DSL routing, separate Generation and Evolution modes, and reviewed knowledge reuse through CAKE Book and a Self-Evolving Agent. On 53 CANN-Bench v1.1 operators on Ascend 950PR, CAKE's aggregated results achieve $100\%$ case pass rate on the standard set (1,060/1,060) and $98.28\%$ on the hidden set (4,167/4,240), with an overall mean score of 78.63 out of 100 and an average performance speedup of $1.334\times$ over the baseline. Evolution then pushes correct operators further: EngramGateFusion cuts aggregate device time by $46.6\%$ over 20 rounds and roughly halves the mean roofline gap. These results offer a practical path toward closing Ascend's AI-for-kernel capability gap.

title: The subcritical accelerating Schwarzschild-Bertotti-Robinson family
abstract: We identify the general finite-$\ell$ neutral Alekseev--Astorino Schwarzschild--Bertotti--Robinson family with the subcritical branch of the independently obtained accelerating Schwarzschild--Bertotti--Robinson solution. The exact scale-free dictionary is \begin{equation*} B^2M^2=\frac{m^2}{b^2+\ell^2},\qquad AM=\frac{m\ell}{b^2+\ell^2},\qquad \frac{A}{B}=\frac{\ell}{\sqrt{b^2+\ell^2}}, \end{equation*} up to the north--south orientation convention. Thus finite real $\ell$ covers precisely the acceleration interval $|A|<|B|$: for $\ell\ne0$ the corresponding OP acceleration parameter is nonzero and the two axial openings are unequal, although no acceleration horizon is present. We establish the identification by canonical Weyl-rod matching and horizon-shape comparison, an independent conicity check, and an exact off-horizon reconstruction of the metric and Maxwell field. The centered limit $\ell=0$ is the nonaccelerating Schwarzschild--BR solution, whereas $|\ell|\to\infty$ approaches the critical boundary $|A/B|=1$ from below. The Astorino parameter $\ell$ therefore parametrizes subcritical acceleration rather than an additional independent neutral black-hole degree of freedom.

title: Reflection symmetry in the equal-mass $1+N$ coorbital problem for $5\leq N\leq8$
abstract: We study reflection symmetry in the equal-mass Newtonian \(1+N\) coorbital problem for \(N=5,6,7,8\). We prove that every collision-free solution of the angular central-configuration equations has a reflection axis. As a consequence, every non-coalescent limit of planar central configurations consisting of one dominant mass and \(N\) equal small masses is reflection-symmetric about a line through the dominant body. Our proof combines analytic arguments with rigorous computer-assisted verification. For each possible reflection, we introduce variables that measure the deviation from that reflection and vanish exactly when the configuration has that symmetry. The central-configuration equations yield a symmetric matrix equation in these variables. Concavity of the force derivative and estimates of the resulting quadratic forms reduce the symmetry problem to finitely many rigorously verified inequalities. Although the details depend on \(N\), the same general method applies in all four cases. We also obtain, as a separate result, the complete three-class classification for \(N=5\), up to the natural equivalences.

title: Stability-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneity-Aware Composite Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) provides a flexible mechanism for adapting traffic signal control to heterogeneous traffic and sensing conditions, but directly learned signal actions do not automatically inherit the analytical properties of structured traffic-control methods. This paper proposes Com-MP, a theory-guided RL framework that learns a context-dependent composition of multiple max-pressure (MP) control preferences while retaining decentralized MP phase selection. The learned policy adapts the relative influence of constituent MP formulations according to local traffic and sensing conditions, allowing data-driven adaptation to operate within a structured traffic-control framework. We show that such intersection-specific and time-varying composition preserves strong queue stability for every demand in the strictly stabilizable region under any admissible non-anticipative composition policy, thereby separating the performance-adaptation role of learning from the stability property of the underlying controller. In a representative implementation combining detector-supported queue-based MP and connected-vehicle-supported travel-time MP, experiments on a real-world 45-intersection network show that Com-MP reduces average delay by 15.6\% and 8.6\% relative to the two constituent controllers, respectively, and by about 7.0\% relative to the best fixed composition. The learned composition responds systematically to local traffic and sensing conditions, remains effective under heterogeneous and degraded sensing, and can be transferred without retraining to an unseen network with an average delay only 2.4\% higher than that of a policy trained directly on the target network. These results show how learning-based adaptation can be introduced within a stability-preserving traffic-control structure, providing a theory-guided pathway toward trustworthy learning-enabled traffic signal control.

title: Multichoice Modeling: Exploring Decision Configuration Space under Uncertainty
abstract: Decision support has become sophisticated at exploring uncertainty, but much less so at representing the architecture of the decision itself. As a result, the decision space is often narrowed before uncertainty is analyzed, leaving interactions among choices and the effects of alternatives they imply largely invisible. This paper introduces multichoice modeling, a framework for making large decision configuration spaces explicit and computationally explorable under uncertainty. Drawing on the logic of rugged landscapes, we conceptualize such problems as contingent performance landscapes, where interdependent choices generate configuration-specific outcomes whose value changes across uncertain futures. The computational framework combines multidimensional decision and uncertainty spaces in a single simulation. Further, variance-based sensitivity analysis is used for identifying influential choices, and conditional distribution analysis for comparing configuration-specific performance profiles. We demonstrate the framework through three case studies: a manufacturing process upgrade, M&A strategy, and mortgage design. By contrasting conventional uncertainty-only analysis with multichoice modeling, the cases show how opening the decision configuration space can reveal unexpected complementarities, near-best configurations with different risk profiles, and strategies that were not apparent as alternatives at the outset.

title: ResGVC: Residual Coding for High-fidelity Generative Video Compression
abstract: Generative video compression (GVC) methods usually employ decoder-side diffusion models to denoise reconstructed signals based on generative priors. Besides, most of these methods perform denoising in latent space rather than directly in pixel domain. In this paper, we propose ResGVC, a residual coding framework for GVC that guides denoising toward original pictures by transmitting residual signals. ResGVC first encodes the original pictures within a learned video codec, and then decomposes the distortion between the codec reconstruction and the original pictures into a sequence of residual segments, where each residual segment is acquired at each denoising step. Residual segments can further be compressed by a novel residual codec with a diffusion transformer as an entropy model. Unlike prior methods, ResGVC introduces explicit source constraints throughout denoising rather than relying on decoder-side generation alone. The diffusion-based entropy model also enables more effective distribution modeling capability based on the powerful generative priors. Moreover, denoising directly in pixel space avoids the irreversible information loss caused by latent representation bottlenecks. Experimental results show that, compared with the previous state-of-the-art method, ResGVC achieves 63.7% and 83.8% BD-rate reductions in terms of LPIPS and PSNR, respectively, while also delivering superior visual quality.

title: Set-theoretic inevitability
abstract: After defining the concept of inevitability for statements with the modal logic of forcing, we raise the question of which statements are inevitable under $\mathsf{ZFC}$ and under large cardinal hypotheses. We show that $\mathsf{SOA}$ (defined as $\mathsf{ZFC}^-$ + $\mathsf V=\mathsf{HC}$) plus the $\boldsymbolΣ^1_2$-perfect set property is $\mathsf{ZFC}$-inevitable, and that Projective Determinacy is inevitable in the theory of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ with a proper class of Woodin cardinals. We then discuss the possible conceptual significance of these results for the foundations of set theory.

title: Algorithmic drift in generative adaptive learning
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence promises to democratize personalized tutoring, yet the longitudinal stability of adaptive systems remains under-theorized. Current ethical discourse focuses on static bias. This paper argues that a distinct threat lies in algorithmic drift: a feedback loop in which minor, demographically asymmetric observation errors compound over time into systemic inequities. We make three contributions. First, we formalize algorithmic drift as a coupled learner--tutor dynamical system. Second, we corroborate this theory with an agent-based Monte Carlo simulation in which either a transparent online tracker or an LSTM deep-knowledge-tracing network drives an IRT-based curriculum policy. Third, we introduce the temporal fairness stabilizer (TFS), a targeted intervention that periodically re-probes learner capability, and benchmark it against standard exploration baselines with explicit group-fairness metrics and replication-level inference. Within the modeled environment, TFS closes the achievement gap where generic exploration does not, and we characterize the conditions under which it succeeds. We separate what is established analytically, what is demonstrated in simulation, and what remains to be validated with real learners. Our results reframe algorithmic fairness in education as a temporal property of a closed loop rather than a deployment-time checkbox.

title: Sequential Monte Carlo Sampling of Feasible Regions Represented by R-Functions
abstract: Feasible-region sampling and volume estimation become increasingly inefficient when constraints define only a small fraction of a convenient bounding domain. We combine R-functions, which encode compound feasibility as a continuous signed field, with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) samplers. The proposed construction exploits not only the sign of the R-function, which determines exact feasibility, but also its continuous negative values outside the feasible set, which provide graded information on constraint violation. Logistic intermediate distributions use this information to guide particles progressively towards feasibility, while the final target distribution remains uniform on the feasible region. Experiments on intersections and unions, including disconnected cases of hyperballs, show substantial variance reductions relative to direct rejection sampling, with the statistical advantage generally increasing as the feasible fraction decreases. For sufficiently small feasible regions, these advantages persist even after accounting for computational cost. To isolate the benefit of continuous R-function information, we also compare the proposed method with an SMC sampler with a region-only (RO) construction that uses the same sequential particle machinery but retains only binary feasible/infeasible information. We demonstrate that the R-function-informed SMC method concentrates particles in the feasible region earlier and produces lower-variance volume estimates than RO.

title: Comparison of the Bergman and Szegő kernels on arbitrary bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
abstract: On every bounded pseudoconvex domain $Ω\Subset\mathbb C^n$, $n\ge2$, with $C^2$ boundary, we prove $K_Ω/S_Ω\le C_{Ω,\varepsilon} δ_Ω^{-1}|\logδ_Ω|^{1+\varepsilon}$ near the boundary for every $\varepsilon>0$, where $δ_Ω$ denotes the boundary distance. For each positive nondecreasing $H(s)=o(s)$, a smoothly bounded pseudoconvex complete Reinhardt domain in $\mathbb C^2$ shows that the logarithmic factor cannot be replaced by $H(|\logδ_Ω|)$.

title: Assessing the consistency of the CPL dark-energy model with cosmological data: Simulation-calibrated neural posterior disagreement
abstract: Recent DESI observations hint at a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state that crosses the phantom divide within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parameterization. In this work, we assess the consistency of the CPL parameterization with current cosmological observations. We develop a model check based on the disagreement between posteriors inferred by neural posterior estimation and flow-matching posterior estimation. Both estimators are trained on the same CPL simulations, and their posterior disagreement is calibrated using independent simulations to obtain a global $p$-value. Controlled simulations assess the reliability of the calibrated \(p\)-values and show how detection sensitivity depends on the form of departure from the assumed model. Applying the test to the compressed CMB+DESI+DESY5 data vector yields $p_{\rm global}=0.524$, indicating that the current observations are consistent with the CPL model. The method has a median evaluation time of only $0.53\,{\rm s}$, enabling efficient assessments of cosmological model adequacy. This framework enables efficient tests of dark-energy models, providing a firmer basis for investigating the physical origin of cosmic acceleration.

title: The Mechanism of Chirality in Plasmonic Structures: Asymmetric Resonance Modes
abstract: This study presents a theoretical framework for understanding the mechanism of chirality generation and circular dichroism (CD) in chiral nanostructures, with a particular focus on the role of asymmetric plasmon resonance mode distributions. Although previous studies have linked chiroptical properties to resonance differences, the specific nature and origin of these differences have not been fully elucidated. Here, we provide a more detailed explanation by quantitatively analyzing the asymmetric electric-field components arising from mode asymmetry. Specifically, we examine the near-field symmetry of individual nanorods and corner-stacked coupled structures (CSCS). The results demonstrate that chirality arises from asymmetric electric-field distributions, which give rise to distinct phase and amplitude responses of the electromagnetic fields in the composite structure under right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) and left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) illumination. The absorption and CD spectra, which exhibit distinct features around $910\,\mathrm{nm}$, support this mechanism and provide valuable insights into the design of chiroptical materials. The proposed mechanism is not restricted to a specific chiral structure or resonance and offers a broader explanation for the generation of circular dichroism.

title: Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters for Utility-Preserving Anti-Distillation
abstract: While reasoning traces improve model capability, they also provide supervision signals for downstream distillation. Initial efforts to mitigate this issue rely on decoding-time interventions, but they incur high inference overhead and can harm the teacher model's natural fluency. We propose Conflict-Aware Logit Adapters (CALA), a lightweight training-time defense. CALA attaches a small residual adapter to a frozen teacher model and trains only the adapter. A proxy student identifies positions where imitation is most sensitive, and the adapter perturbs the output distribution at these positions while remaining within high-probability regions. A conflict-aware optimization strategy balances anti-distillation and utility objectives, while regularization preserves the teacher's performance and fluency. At inference time, CALA incurs modest overhead and requires no auxiliary model. Experiments on reasoning benchmarks show that CALA substantially reduces successful student imitation while maintaining near-original teacher performance and generation quality. These results establish CALA as a practical and efficient alternative to decoding-time approaches.

title: Harm Is Behavioural, Moderation Is Lexical: How Language and Culture Decide Whom Automated Safety Systems Protect and Whom They Silence
abstract: Content warning: this paper quotes slurs and hateful statements from published test suites; the racial slur among them is masked. Automated systems decide at scale which messages are harmful, and they decide unevenly. Classifiers label African American English as offensive up to twice as often as other English, the accounts of prominent drag queens can score as more toxic than those of white nationalists, and safety behaviour that holds in English collapses in low-resource languages. We argue that over-flagging and under-protection share one cause: deciding harm from vocabulary and surface form rather than from what a message does. We organise the evidence into seven failure modes and argue, as testable hypotheses, that harmful behaviours (a request for secrecy, a demand for payment, an attempt to isolate someone) travel across languages better than the words that express them. We propose an evaluation protocol that makes the gap between the best- and worst-served language communities a headline result, and show that the naive gap is inflated under equal service and that its usual bootstrap interval is unreliable. Applied to five open systems in eleven languages, from a keyword lexicon to two current multilingual guard models, the protocol finds that none reaches native-speaker accuracy at separating harmful function from harmless form (51 of 55 system-language pairs fall short); that greater capability raises discrimination in nine languages while leaving Arabic and romanised Hindi near chance, so the gap between the best- and worst-served languages grows with capability; that one system both over-flags and under-protects the same language most; and that a language a system reads worst can look the most fairly treated when only false positives are reported.

title: Directing to Diversify: Multi-Directional Search for Automatic Heuristic Design
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong potential to automate heuristic design for NP-hard combinatorial optimization (CO) tasks without human intervention. Recent methods predominantly rely on evolutionary computation (EC) frameworks, where heuristic diversification is mainly induced through EC-like operators or downstream selection, while the direction of heuristic transformation remains largely unharnessed. In this paper, we propose a multi-directional Perturbation-Rewrite Search (PRS) framework for automatic heuristic design that factorizes heuristic transformation through directional search primitives at the generation level. Specifically, PRS operates on heuristic ideas through three complementary directions: expansion toward richer and more expressive designs, compression toward simpler and less specialized designs, and steering for fine-grained refinement, together enabling broader and more sustained exploration of diverse regions in the heuristic design space. PRS further organizes candidate exploration within a breadth-first search-based process with adaptive operator control, which ensures thorough candidate utilization and sustained exploration, and maintains strong search dynamics while preventing premature convergence. Extensive empirical results across diverse CO tasks show that PRS consistently discovers high-quality heuristics, demonstrating the effectiveness and generality of explicitly directional exploration design.

title: The Keller-Segel Model for Chemotaxis on Metapopulation Graphs and Graphons
abstract: Many models of spatial populations use directed motion towards environmental attractants as a mechanism for spatial pattern formation. While prior approaches typically focus on partial differential equation models for directed motion in continuous space, it is natural to consider the dynamics of biological and social systems on a metapopulation featuring well-mixed local patches and spatial motion between patches. In this paper, we formulate a version of the Keller-Segel model for chemotaxis on a graph metapopulation, modeling a chemoattractant that can diffuse across patches and a population of individuals who move through a biased random walk through comparing chemoattractant levels along edges of the metapopulation network. We also derive a continuum limit for our model describing chemotaxis in a population on patches connected by a graphon, showing that our resulting integro-differential equation model arises as the limit of our discrete patch model for families of large deterministic or random graphs. Through linear stability analysis, we derive conditions on the chemotactic sensitivity required to produce instability of a spatially uniform equilibrium for our Keller-Segel models in terms of the reaction parameters and the eigenvalues of the Laplacian operator for the metapopulation graph or graphon. Through a mix of weakly nonlinear stability analysis, numerical simulations, and analytical bounds on solutions, we can also characterize the form of pattern-forming instability in our graphon model and show how our choice of demographic dynamics for the population and the graphon adjacency function can impact the long-time total population size and chemoattractant concentration achieved in emergent spatial patterns.

title: Adaptive Uncertainty Visualization With jk-Plots
abstract: An important task of uncertainty visualizations is to communicate how the number of available observations influences the precision of estimates, such as a Normal distribution's mean. In this paper, we propose an adaptive approach to visualizing univariate data that produces salient representations while highlighting the uncertainty introduced by the sample size. We introduce jk-plots, inspired by educational material of Bayesian statistics, that combine visualizations of plausible reference models (emulating popular uncertainty visualization idioms) and the observations. We describe a visualization pipeline to create jk-plots, which we implemented in an R package. We demonstrate jk-plots using synthetic datasets of varying size and discuss possible usage scenarios in domain expert interviews.

title: Tilt-Rotor Quadcopter with Learned Residual Control and Mode-Dependent State Estimation
abstract: Tilt-rotor quadcopters redirect thrust for translation without banking, but complicate modeling, state estimation, and disturbance rejection. This paper presents a simulation-based flight stack for a \SI{2.00}{\kilo\gram} tilt-rotor quadcopter. The system uses a six-degree-of-freedom nonlinear model with first-order motor dynamics and two-axis rotor tilt, parameterized using a 3D CAD model. A cascaded PD controller commands forward and lateral tilt angles. A 14-state EKF fuses sensor data across hover, early-transition, and transition modes using a hysteretic (Schmitt-trigger) classifier to prevent covariance discontinuities. Because the proportional position loop leaves a steady-state offset under constant wind, a small bounded neural residual is added on top of the unmodified PD controller. It is trained by behavioral cloning from a teacher with privileged access to the true wind, while the deployed network never observes wind. In simulation, the EKF achieves a post-settling position root mean square error (RMSE) of \SI{0.226}{\metre} (horizontal) and \SI{0.03}{\metre} (vertical) and an attitude RMSE below \SI{0.8}{\degree}, and it estimates a wind velocity of $(\num{2.0}, \num{-1.2})\,\unit{\metre\per\second}$ to within \SI{0.15}{\metre\per\second} per axis. The residual reduces steady-state station-keeping error under wind by approximately \SI{49}{\percent}, from \SI{0.117}{\metre} to \SI{0.060}{\metre} at \SI{1.5}{\metre\per\second} and from \SI{0.319}{\metre} to \SI{0.162}{\metre} at an out-of-distribution \SI{3.9}{\metre\per\second}. The framework provides a basis for hardware-in-the-loop and flight-test studies.

title: There is no universal $F_σ$ equivalence relation
abstract: Rosendal proved that any $K_σ$ equivalence relation is Borel reducible to $\ell_\infty$. We prove that for every $F_σ$ equivalence relation $F$ on a Polish space, there is an $F_σ$ real linear subspace $H$ of $\ell_2$ such that the coset relation $x\mathrel{E_H}y$ if and only if $x-y\in H$ has no Baire-measurable reduction to $F$. In particular, there is no $F_σ$ equivalence relation universal under Borel reducibility for all $F_σ$ equivalence relations. This answers a question of Rosendal.

title: Spatial scaling of network length and shared-node density in bilayer distribution grids
abstract: Certain distribution networks are built in layers, each layer collecting a commodity from the layer above it and delivering it to the layer below. We propose a minimal model that gives the length of each layer per unit area from the local density of demand, here the population density. Starting from the Beardwood, Halton and Hammersley law for minimal networks, the length of a layer depends on the number of nodes it reaches and on the area occupied by the users. When two consecutive layers share this area, the gap between their two length exponents is fixed by the exponent of the density of their shared nodes, with no adjusted parameter. We test the model on the complete low and medium-voltage grid of metropolitan France, at the resolution of a population raster. The exponents are fitted by Poisson maximum likelihood on every pixel, with confidence intervals from a spatial block bootstrap. The length exponents imply an effective settled area that grows sublinearly with the density, and the gap between them agrees with the exponent of the substation density, counted independently. The agreement holds over the whole territory, so that the model can serve to estimate the length of such networks where only the density of demand is known.

title: Cross-Region Cooperation of UAV Swarms Towards Air-Ground ISAC via Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: The limited communication resources and sensing perspectives of a single uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) motivate UAV swarms for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in air-ground networks. However, in multi-region scenarios, regional UAV allocations may not match vehicle demand, while local observations may lack sufficient diversity for accurate sensing. To address these issues, this paper proposes a cross-region cooperation framework for UAV swarms. For communication, cross-region UAV reallocation reduces service disparities by matching resources to vehicle demand. For sensing, combining UAV observations from different regions increases observation diversity, while adaptive handshaking guided by marginal Cramér--Rao bound (CRB) utilities balances phase synchronization gains against handshaking energy consumption. Joint optimization of UAV positions and transmit power within each region then further improves communication service and sensing performance. These coupled decisions are coordinated by a hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (H-MARL) approach through slow-timescale inter-region UAV reallocation and fast-timescale intra-region UAV control. Under the considered simulation settings, reallocation can improve quality of service (QoS) by over 20 percentage points compared with retaining the initial allocation under severe resource-demand mismatches. Cooperative sensing with adaptive handshaking incurs only about a 5.0% increase in mean CRB relative to perfect synchronization.

title: Wandering exposed Julia components of rational maps
abstract: We prove that every wandering exposed Julia component of a rational map is a point. Here a Julia component is exposed if it meets the boundary of a Fatou domain. The theorem extends the corresponding result for polynomials to rational maps, without any assumption on critical recurrence. The proof combines an enhanced nest with a covering estimate for multiply connected pullback domains.

title: Pigeonhole Equal Subset Sum: Subexponential Algorithm, Tight Lower Bounds, and Average-Case Analysis
abstract: The Equal Subset Sum problem asks, given n positive integers bounded by M, to find two distinct non-empty subsets with the same sum. We study this problem in the regime $M = 2^{o(n)}$, where the pigeonhole principle guarantees that a solution exists, and the main challenge is to find one efficiently. A straightforward dynamic-programming algorithm runs in time poly(n).$M$. After a sequence of improvements, the current best algorithm, due to Jin, Williams, and Zhang (ESA 2025), achieves running time poly(n).$M^{1/3}$. In this work, we give the first poly(n).$M^{o(1)}$-time algorithm for Equal Subset Sum in the regime $M = 2^{o(n)}$. We complement this algorithmic result with a tight conditional lower bound showing that any substantial improvement would require a major breakthrough in approximation algorithms for lattice problems, building on recent techniques of Vafa and Vaikuntanathan (STOC 2025). Finally, we show that our techniques yield an asymptotically faster algorithm for the regime when $M = Θ(2^{n})$: a poly(n)$\cdot 2^{n/4}$-time algorithm in the average case.

title: Initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations
abstract: We study initial-boundary value problems for linear lattice differential equations on the half-line. We first give a systematic account of fundamental solutions for equations with general finite-range interactions. We then develop complementary approaches based on reflection, the Laplace transform, and the unified transform method, obtaining contour integral and Bessel-function representations of solutions. For the semidiscrete diffusion equation, we justify these representations for continuous boundary data and initial data of polynomial growth, establish uniqueness in the corresponding growth class, and derive spatial estimates and long-time properties, including asymptotic periodicity. We also treat nonhomogeneous equations, Robin boundary conditions, nonsymmetric coefficients, and a class of time-dependent coefficients. Finally, higher-order examples illustrate how the unified transform approach extends beyond second-order equations.

title: Complete conformal metrics of constant positive scalar curvature with prescribed isolated singularities
abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$ with positive Yamabe constant. For any prescribed finite set $Λ\subset M$ containing at least two points, we construct a complete metric on $M\setminusΛ$, conformal to $g$, with scalar curvature $n(n-1)$. At each singularity, the local geometric term in the reduced action comes from the first nonzero homogeneous metric term of degree at most $(n-2)/2$ in finite conformal normal coordinates, or from the mass of the Green function metric when all such terms vanish. We completely solve Schoen's conjecture about singular Yamabe problem.

title: Topological preservation under aggregation of quantale-valued metric spaces
abstract: Aggregation functions provide a general mechanism for combining multiple inputs into a single output and constitute a fundamental tool in information fusion. Beyond the classical numerical setting, aggregation can also be considered at the level of mathematical structures, where the main question is to determine which properties of the original structures are preserved by the aggregation process. In this paper, we study the preservation of topology within a unified framework based on continuous quantales and quantale-enriched categories. We introduce strongly preserving functions, for which the natural topology induced by a $\mathscr V$-metric space coincides with that induced after aggregation. We decompose this property into its upper and lower versions and show that upper strong preservation is equivalent to Scott continuity at the unit of the domain quantale, whereas lower strong preservation is characterized in terms of the fibre of the unit and the Scott upper semicontinuity of the inverse multifunction. Combining these results, we obtain a complete characterization of strongly preserving functions, together with analogous results for separated, symmetric, and separated and symmetric $\mathscr V$-metric spaces. Finally, we specialize the general theory to functions from $\mathsf P_+^{\,I}$ to $\mathsf P_+$, obtaining characterizations of strongly extended quasi-pseudometric and pseudometric aggregation functions on Cartesian products and on common underlying sets, together with corresponding results for extended quasi-metric and metric aggregation functions on Cartesian products.

title: Diagnosing the Explicit-to-Applied Theory of Mind Gap in LLMs
abstract: As large language models are deployed in high-stakes roles such as therapy, education, and personal assistance, their social cognition must be assessed reliably. Current Theory of Mind (ToM) benchmarks report aggregate scores that conflate two distinct competencies: explicit ToM (recognizing what someone believes) and applied ToM (using that belief to predict behavior). Building on this distinction, we investigate the gap and its recoverability using four structurally diverse benchmarks. Aggregate reporting obscures uneven competence: on SimpleToM, Llama-3.1-8B scores 51.5 percent overall while recognizing mental states at 99.4 percent and predicting behavior at only 28.9 percent. To assess recovery, we compare structured prompting, matched in-context learning, and our proposed Belief-State Test-Time Training (BSTTT), which adapts lightweight parameters on answered support questions through action reconstruction. Across Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, and GPT-oss-20B, recovery depends on the model, task, and intervention. On SimpleToM, reminders combined with BSTTT improve Llama's behavior prediction by 40.8 percentage points; reminders account for most of the overall improvement, with BSTTT adding 1.3 to 5.5 points beyond reminders across models. Contextual examples often outperform weight updates, while BSTTT remains stronger in specific model-benchmark settings. Temporal belief tracking remains difficult despite partial recovery. These findings show that aggregate ToM scores can overstate applied competence while hiding performance recoverable through targeted assistance. We recommend decomposed reporting of explicit and applied accuracy alongside intervention comparisons that establish which failures are recoverable and under what conditions.

title: Safety-constrained position tracking of a flexible transmission system
abstract: We consider safety-constrained position tracking for a flexible transmission system consisting of a torsional shaft driven by a motor and connected to a gravitationally loaded inertia. The coupled PDE-ODE dynamics admit a semilinear formulation in which the linear input-output system is impedance passive and the gravitational torque enters as a bounded, globally Lipschitz perturbation. We establish an energy dissipation inequality for the nonlinear model and show that a position-funnel controller with supervised damping admits a unique global closed-loop trajectory. In particular, the motor-angle tracking error remains strictly inside a prescribed time-varying funnel, which can be chosen to enforce safety bounds on the motor angle.

title: SCOPE: Compiling Natural-Language Policies into Neurosymbolic Predicate Programs
abstract: Policy enforcement for LLM agents has shifted from single-turn content moderation to compound, application-specific policies evaluated over multi-turn transcripts and tool-call trajectories. Fine-tuned guardrail models are efficient but degrade on compound policies, and while LLM-as-a-judge approaches achieve higher accuracy, they incur high inference cost and tend to produce unstable predictions. Neurosymbolic methods offer a natural alternative, decomposing the policy into narrow neural decisions composed under explicit logic. However, existing symbolic layers lack the required expressiveness and are optimized against fixed data rather than the policy itself. To address this, we introduce SCOPE, which compiles a policy into an executable program of neural predicates executed by small models, deterministic extractors, and code that composes their outputs. The program is optimized jointly with its training data, using adversarial generation of counterexamples that target where the program deviates from the policy. We evaluate SCOPE on a benchmark of real-world policy tasks against prompt optimization, task decomposition, and workflow generation methods, achieving the highest average accuracy across tasks and models. Programs optimized with the weakest executor transfer to other models without further optimization. This allows them to be deployed in production on inexpensive models, where they reach accuracy comparable to frontier reasoning models. Unlike these monolithic models, SCOPE produces substantially more stable predictions, and each verdict is interpretable through the predicate outputs that produced it. Additionally, we validate the key components of our method through an ablation study. SCOPE thus enables reliable, interpretable, and efficient policy enforcement at production scale.

title: A unified quantitative approach to Chiti and Kohler--Jobin inequalities
abstract: We obtain two quantitative results related to classical rearrangement inequalities for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue. The first one is a quantitative version of Chiti's reverse Hölder inequality. More precisely, for every $1\le q<p<\infty$, we prove that the deficit controls, up to translations, the $L^q$ distance between a first eigenfunction of a bounded domain and the first eigenfunction of the ball having the same first eigenvalue. The second result concerns the Kohler--Jobin inequality and gives a quantitative estimate in terms of the $L^\infty\!\to L^2$ distance between the corresponding Dirichlet resolvents. In both cases, the main idea is to find a suitable superlevel set of the first eigenfunction which is almost optimal for the Faber-Krahn inequality.

title: AstroBench: Benchmarking Free-Floating Capture and Space Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Capturing a loose object inside a spacecraft requires a robot to approach a target that can translate and rotate, and whose motion changes when contact is made. These conditions motivate evaluation beyond manipulation of supported objects. We introduce AstroBench, an open benchmark for free-floating capture and space robotic manipulation with a fixed-base arm. The task suite combines four initial-motion tracks with sample-storage operations based on MELFI hardware and cap and captive-screw servicing based on the Robotic Refueling Mission. The two workcells provide nine task definitions and 29 task-target combinations. A metadata-filtered Objaverse inventory supplies 8,414 object instances for asset expansion, alongside five cabin visual contexts and versioned task instructions. We report two acquisition-focused experiments using existing checkpoints. A frozen $π_{0.5}$ DROID joint-position policy captures 2 of 200 static targets and 4 of 200 moving targets across twenty object identities. A cube-specific ACT policy captures 8 of 10 static targets and 6 of 10 moving targets in a separate experiment. Each experiment retains its recorded observation, action and capture configuration. The results document difficult direct transfer for the tested generalist checkpoint and successful task-specific capture behavior, while identifying concrete settings for studying motion-aware perception and contact-sensitive control. Code, task definitions and editable workcell assets are available at https://github.com/AstroUpLab/AstroBench.

title: A General-Purpose Dual-Path Interaction Framework for Multi-View Medical Image Segmentation: Alleviating Data Volume Dependency in Small-Sample Regimes
abstract: The performance of medical image segmentation depends on a large amount of annotated data, and most segmentation models experience a significant drop in performance in low-sample-size scenarios. Existing semi-supervised and weakly supervised methods rely on specific network architectures, while traditional multi-view-assisted segmentation methods require strictly paired samples, which limits their clinical applications. To address these issues, we propose DPIF, a general-purpose plug-and-play dual-path interaction framework compatible with arbitrary encoder-decoder segmentation networks, which leverages cross-view anatomical complementarity to reduce annotation reliance. DPIF first performs Sinkhorn optimal transport-based cross-view distribution alignment to establish global semantic correspondence without sample-level pairing. It then adopts conditional mutual information-guided feature decoupling to enable bidirectional knowledge transfer only within the shared semantic space, suppressing view-specific noise. Finally, persistent homology-based topological regularization encodes anatomical invariants as unsupervised priors to mitigate overfitting. Experiments were conducted using 24 baseline models on a private multicenter echocardiography dataset and two public datasets. The results show that DPIF-enhanced models outperform single-view baseline models when trained on comparable amounts of data. Notably, most dual-path variants trained on 40\% - 60\% of the data achieve performance comparable to that of single-view models trained on the full dataset. This demonstrates that DPIF provides a general-purpose and scalable solution for data-scarce multi-view medical image segmentation problems.

title: Dual Exam: Controlled Evaluation of Multimodal Agents and World Models
abstract: World Models (WMs) can support Multimodal Agents (MAs) through simulated experience, while Agent trajectories can inform World Model refinement. Evaluating this interaction requires separate evidence about action selection and state evolution. We introduce Dual Exam, which tests Agents under fixed environment response mechanisms and World Models under fixed action interventions across physical, digital, social, and scientific domains. The Agent track compares 10 configurations on 1,088 items in 15 reporting categories. The World Model track contains 400 cases across eight scenarios; 15 configurations have full coverage and one covers six scenarios. GPT 6 Astra leads the case-weighted Agent Index at 31.3, and GPT-Image-2 leads the full-coverage WM Overall at 21.7. These scores use different tasks and metrics and are not directly comparable. A 150-case pilot of one coupled pairing records zero task successes and motivates component-level diagnosis. Results reveal uneven task performance and failures to preserve task-relevant state. Their value for predicting coupled success or sustained reciprocal learning remains to be established.

title: Scale-free localization in pseudo-Hermitian quantum walk
abstract: Scale-free localization is a distinctive phenomenon in non-Hermitian systems, where specific eigenstates, known as scale-free localized states (LSs), possess localization lengths that scale linearly with the system size. Here, we show that a single non-Hermitian defect in one-dimensional quantum walks (QWs) induces scale-free localization. Driven by non-Hermiticity, the QW system undergoes a pseudo-Hermitian (PH) phase transition and the PH symmetry breaking is accompanied by the emergence of scale-free localization. As non-Hermiticity is further increased, the system undergoes a second phase transition, marked by the emergence of two pairs of bound states. Crucially, we identify the critical points of both transitions using localization properties. Furthermore, we extend our investigation to two-dimensional QWs, where a single non-Hermitian defect also induces scale-free localization, thereby demonstrating the universality of this phenomenon. Our work provides a valuable perspective for further exploring defect physics and a type of novel LS in non-Hermitian quantum systems.

title: On global Chern-Calabi flows on compact complex surfaces
abstract: In this paper, we propose the Chern-Calabi Flow for extremal metrics in conformal Hermitian geometry. After the existence of extremal metric, we consider the existence of global flows to the Chern-Calabi flows for extremal metrics on compact complex surfaces with Gauduchon metrics. To achieve this goal, we use the Adams inequality and the Gronwall inequality method to obtain fourth order derivative norm estimates. We also study the convergence of the global solution to the Chern-Calabi flow and its limit is the solution of the Chern-Calabi extremal metric problem. We propose a fourth order elliptic problem and derive the Bochner formula relevant to the elliptic estimates for the Chern-Calabi heat flow.

title: Federated Differentially Private Optimization via Low-Rank Preconditioning
abstract: We consider differentially private (DP) optimization in the federated setting, where a DP estimate of the feature covariance matrix serves as a Hessian approximation for generalized linear models. Existing central DP methods for covariance estimation have communication cost that grows quadratically in the data dimension, while existing baselines with linear communication cost are only locally private and degrade as the number of clients increases. As a remedy, we propose a federated DP-PCA framework that achieves linear communication cost while providing central DP guarantees under secure aggregation. It consists of a DP rank selection step, a DP power method, and a noisy release of the covariance projected onto the selected low-dimensional subspace. We give error bounds for this covariance estimate and for the resulting low-communication preconditioned DP gradient descent. Empirically, our proposed DP optimization method matches a centralized baseline with quadratic communication cost at a fraction of the communication.

title: Norm-Aware Product Formulas for Hamiltonian Simulations
abstract: With the target of efficiently solving the quantum-mechanical Schrödinger equation on future quantum computers, first- and second-order product formulas for the time-evolution operator are proposed, designed to exploit hierarchies in the operator norms of the individual Hamiltonian components. Inspired by the THRIFT product formula, these decomposition schemes achieve a suppression of the leading error term by a factor of alpha<1 with respect to the standard Lie--Trotter--Suzuki splitting of the same order, where alpha quantifies the norm ratio between the dominant and subdominant parts of the Hamiltonian. Unlike THRIFT, the proposed formulas retain the general product-formula structure, making them applicable to Hamiltonians whose terms act on an arbitrary number of qubits. The advantages of this approach are demonstrated through numerical experiments on engineered two-dimensional spin-1/2 XY model systems and isolated molecules within the double-factorization framework.

title: Conditional Mean Flows for Frequency-Domain Scattered Wavefield Generation
abstract: Frequency-domain wavefield modeling underpins seismic imaging and inversion, where repeated Helmholtz solutions become costly as velocity models, source locations, and frequencies vary. Neural operators learn mappings between physical fields, and their accuracy can decline outside the training distribution. Diffusion models learn wavefield distributions and generally require repeated sampling evaluations to produce accurate fields. A conditional mean flows model is introduced for complex scattered-wavefield generation. The analytical background wavefield serves as a condition alongside the velocity model, supplying spatially organized information about the source location and frequency. Learning the scattered wavefield avoids the point-source singularity in the target and supports generalization across these physical conditions. The model estimates the average transport velocity over a finite interval connecting Gaussian noise to the scattered field. This representation captures the accumulated displacement and permits both full-interval one-step generation and interval-partitioned sampling. Trained on OpenFWI, the model is evaluated on in-distribution and out-of-distribution velocity structures, frequency generalization, and inference efficiency. In most evaluated settings, one-step mean flows sampling achieves lower wavefield error than multi-step diffusion. Because each sampling step requires another network evaluation, accurate one-step generation also reduces inference time. These results indicate that mean flows can provide accurate and efficient frequency-domain scattered-wavefield generation.

title: Extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method
abstract: Regularized lattice Boltzmann methods improve numerical stability by projecting the nonequilibrium distribution onto its hydrodynamic second-order Hermite sector and filtering the remaining kinetic modes. We introduce a separate relaxation time for the complete complementary kinetic subspace. The resulting extended-regularized lattice Boltzmann method (E-RLBM) interpolates continuously between the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and regularized collision operators while retaining a two-rate implementation. A Chapman-Enskog expansion shows that the isothermal Navier-Stokes equations are recovered with kinematic viscosity $ν=c_s^2(τ-Δt/2)$, independently of the kinetic relaxation time $τ_{\rm nh}$, whereas $τ_{\rm nh}$ changes higher-order truncation errors. For linear transverse shear, its first effect is a fourth-derivative term whose coefficient depends on the direction of propagation relative to the lattice. This fourth-order coefficient is affine in $τ_{\rm nh}$. For linear shear on D2Q9 and $τ_{\rm nh}$ between $τ$ and $Δt$, it lies between the corresponding BGK and RLBM values in every propagation direction. Stability maps for the decaying Taylor-Green vortex and flow past a rectangular obstacle show that an appropriate kinetic relaxation substantially enlarges the stable parameter domain. In a Taylor-Green convergence test with consistent initialization, all three operators converge at second order, and their error differences follow the hyperviscous coefficient for diagonal shear waves: the E-RLBM error is about 6% above the BGK error and about 40% below the RLBM error; in a double shear layer at Re = 80000, the E-RLBM follows the RLBM convergence curve. The proposed collision operator therefore provides a low-cost means of controlling nonhydrodynamic modes without introducing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.

title: The classification of smooth 3-fold flops
abstract: This paper establishes the analytic classification of smooth, simple, 3-fold flops, and in the process provides both an intrinsic characterisation and a classification of their contraction algebras.

title: Directionally Correct Views in Portfolio Optimization
abstract: Portfolio optimization techniques often use historical data to estimate parameters for Markowitz-type or ML models. Effective allocation requires a way to align the available data with conditions expected over the investment horizon. Inspired by the Black-Litterman framework, we ask whether incorporating expert views leads to better portfolio allocations. In a simple Markowitz setting, we show that even a small amount of directionally correct information can materially improve investment decisions. We also discuss how expert views can be incorporated in end-to-end portfolio models using entropy-based ideas. Somewhat surprisingly, our empirical results indicate that simpler Markowitz-type model perform as well as an end-to-end model, once directionally correct experts are incorporated.

title: When Forgotten Facts Return: Relearning-Aware Unlearning of Knowledge Graph Embeddings via Tangent Kernels
abstract: Approximate unlearning answers a deletion request on a knowledge-graph embedding by editing entity embeddings instead of retraining from scratch. These embeddings keep being updated as new facts arrive. Under this ordinary continued training, forgotten facts recover more than in the exact-unlearning baseline, a model retrained without them and given the same continued training. We trace this relearning to entity embeddings shared by forgotten and new facts. To our knowledge, this is the first study of relearning in knowledge-graph embeddings. Relearning-robust methods developed for deep networks do not account for the graph structure underlying this recovery. We propose Kernel-Anticipated Unlearning (KAU), which uses the tangent kernel to model how continued training changes forgotten facts' scores through these shared parameters. KAU expresses this first-order response in closed form and differentiates through it inside the forgetting loss. The objective steers edits toward directions that continued training reverses less. We compare KAU with state-of-the-art knowledge-graph unlearners and relearning-robust methods under identical continued training, measuring leakage beyond the exact-unlearning baseline. Across three backbones, KAU reduces the strongest knowledge-graph unlearner's leakage by 46-63% on FB15k-237 and 50-82% on CoDEx-L, at higher retained utility.

title: A precise TESS ephemeris for the short-period binary TIC-259864042
abstract: This paper presents a precise eclipse-timing analysis of TIC 259864042 (= EC 02406--6408, Gaia DR3 4647004122914240640) using eleven sectors of TESS photometry spanning 2018--2025 (7.1 yr). The system exhibits a single deep eclipse with a V-shaped profile at phase 0 and no detectable counterpart at phase 0.5. Four independent period-search methods converge to a common period agreeing to within 7 parts per million. An independent reduction with the SHERLOCK pipeline, using its own 120-second TESS photometry, confirms the same period at the same precision. A joint linear ephemeris fit gives P = 0.46048676 $\pm$ 0.0000001 d (11.059 h) and T_0 = 2458325.70381 $\pm$ 0.00002 BJD, with a residual RMS of 0.87 min across the 7.1-yr baseline. Per-sector ephemeris fits show residual medians within $\pm$0.42 min of zero, confirming that no cycle slip has occurred across the large TESS data gaps. The period is stable at the level of $Δ$BIC = +5.21 (in favour of the constant-period model); an upper limit of $|\dot{P}| \le 1 \times 10^{-9}$ d d$^{-1}$ is placed on any secular period change. A PHOEBE 2.4 fit to the Sector 27 light curve yields $i = 80.8^{\circ} \pm 0.5^{\circ}$, $R_1 = 0.21 \pm 0.01\ R_{\odot}$, $R_2 = 0.25 \pm 0.02\ R_{\odot}$, $q = 0.49 \pm 0.07$, consistent with a grazing detached geometry and a mid-M-dwarf companion. The TESS light curve alone cannot distinguish between the two temperatures 25100 K and 31000 K. The paper discusses the system in the context of the sdB eclipsing binary population, and notes that while the current data are consistent with a short-period sdB+M-dwarf architecture, a phase-resolved spectrum is needed to independently confirm the sdB identification.

title: In situ performance of the Vertex Silicon Plane in the BM@N experiment during Run 9
abstract: The Vertex Silicon Plane (VSP) was commissioned and operated for the first time as the most upstream tracking station of the Baryonic Matter at Nuclotron (BM@N) experiment at the NICA accelerator complex during Run 9. The station consisting of six double-sided silicon microstrip modules based on the CBM-BM@N detector technology was installed about 8 cm downstream from the target inside the SP-41 analyzing magnet. The in situ module performance was characterized in terms of the signal-to-noise ratio, time resolution, and Lorentz drift in the magnetic field. The most probable cluster signal-to-noise ratio ranges from 15.5 to 33.2, while the time resolution relative to the trigger pulse is about 12 ns. The tracking performance was evaluated using track-hit residuals and hit-matching efficiency; two independent reference configurations based on the Forward Silicon Detector (FSD) and Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) tracking systems give consistent efficiencies of about 95%. The contribution of the VSP to the BM@N tracking performance was further studied through the transverse track impact parameter and the reconstruction of short VSP-GEM tracklets. Owing to its position close to the target and its coverage at large polar angles, the VSP provides an additional near-target tracking point and makes it possible to extend the geometrical acceptance beyond that of the FSD- and GEM-based central tracking system.

title: Self-Supervised Representation Learning for JWST Galaxy Images and Low Resolution Spectra
abstract: A self-supervised multimodal model recovers galaxy stellar masses from sparse JWST data that lack the multi-band coverage required by traditional SED fitting. We train on single-band F150W imaging paired with observed-frame 1-2 $μ$m PRISM spectra and obtain a joint image-spectrum representation that recovers stellar mass at $1<z\le3$ with $R^2 \sim 0.9$ and $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.24$ dex; cross-modal CLIP alignment further raises single-modality performance by $ΔR^2 = +0.04$ (imaging) and $+0.09$ (spectroscopy), narrowing the gap to joint-modality inference. The code and documentation are available at \href{https://github.com/2003cy/neurips2026_ssl_jwst}{GitHub}.

title: The taming of 3-fold flops
abstract: This article overviews recent progress in understanding and classifying one of the most elementary of birational surgeries within algebraic geometry, namely 3-fold flops, through the development of a noncommutative version of singularity theory.

title: nnInteractive Agent: General-Purpose AI Agents as 3D Image Annotators
abstract: Interactive 3D segmentation models such as nnInteractive turn a few spatial prompts (points, scribbles, boxes) into accurate volumetric masks, but a human still does the annotation work: finding each structure, placing prompts, checking the result and correcting it. General-purpose AI agents can now interpret images, call tools and write code. We show that such agents can take over this work without additional training: the user makes a request in plain language, and the agent works out what has to be segmented, locates the targets, prompts nnInteractive, inspects the 3D result, corrects it and responds to feedback. Asked for 'the muscles used for chewing', an agent identifies and segments the masseters and pterygoids; asked to count liver lesions, it writes its own code to find candidates and splits a merged lesion on request. Our open-source nninteractive-agent provides nnInteractive as tools over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), together with a skill that encodes how experienced users prompt it. On a benchmark spanning CT, MRI, PET and micro-CT of humans, a mouse and an ant (14 images; 51 targets from organs and tumours to muscles, foot bones, vessel trees and an insect brain), Claude Code and Codex reach a mean Dice of 0.81 and 0.84 from the request alone; when told where each target is, both reach 0.85 and prompt nearly as effectively as an oracle that places prompts using the reference segmentation. A text-prompted 3D model (VoxTell) is more accurate on most standard radiological targets but less robust: it returns an empty mask for one of them and fails on the leg muscles, the foot bones, the mouse and the ant, where the agents remain accurate. Code: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nninteractive-agent

title: Cosmological Inference with Gravitational-Wave Dark Sirens and 21-cm Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA with MeerKAT and SKAO
abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) and 21-cm intensity mapping (IM) are emerging as complementary cosmological probes: GWs provide direct luminosity-distance measurements, while neutral-hydrogen (HI) IM traces the matter distribution in redshift space. Their synergy offers a promising avenue for precise measurements of the Hubble constant. Within a standard-siren framework, we perform a joint cosmological and population analysis using $\mathcal{O}(150)$ mock GW detections with SNR > 12, as projected for one year of observations at LVK O5 sensitivity. We combine these with mock HI intensity maps from MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, and study how observational limitations in both the GW and IM data affect the $H_0$ constraints. We find that uncertainty in GW parameter measurements is a dominant limitation on the cosmological constraints. Neglecting this uncertainty, the inclusion of HI information enables sub-percent constraints on $H_0$. We also find that observational effects in the HI surveys weaken the constraints, although they remain tighter than those obtained without HI information (spectral sirens). Despite accounting for HI IM observational limitations, including HI information reduces the $H_0$ uncertainty relative to the spectral-siren results by 61% for MeerKLASS and 53% for SKA-Mid. Because our results are based on a single realisation, they should be interpreted in light of possible realisation-to-realisation variability. Beam convolution most severely weakens the constraints. Instrumental noise can induce multimodality in the posterior, potentially biasing the inferred parameters. The results are sensitive to foreground under-cleaning and over-cleaning. Partial sky coverage has a relatively small impact. In the most realistic scenario, which accounts for both GW and HI IM limitations, we obtain $H_0$ precision estimates of 10% and 15% for MeerKLASS and SKA-Mid, respectively.

title: Potential estimates and improved Sobolev regularity for nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations
abstract: This paper investigates pointwise and oscillatory potential estimates for viscosity solutions and their gradients to a class of nonlocal fully nonlinear elliptic equations. The key ingredient of our argument is to establish precise pointwise bounds for a novel fractional sharp maximal function defined in terms of affine functions. As an immediate consequence, we prove higher order Sobolev regularity results of Calderón-Zygmund type for such equations without imposing any global boundedness assumptions on viscosity solutions. The potential theory developed herein extends the work of Daskalopoulos-Kuusi-Mingione (Commun. Partial Differ. Equ. 39: 574-590, 2014) for fully nonlinear second order elliptic equations to the fractional fully nonlinear setting.

title: MQAScore: Fine-Grained Text-Music Alignment Evaluation via Large Audio Language Model
abstract: Text-to-music alignment is commonly evaluated by the global similarity between text and audio embeddings, which collapses all described attributes into a single score and obscures which ones are missing. We instead introduce MQAScore, which verifies each atomic musical concept along five clip-level dimensions (genre, instrument, mood/theme, vocal, and usage) by the probability that a large audio language model (LALM) answers affirmatively to a binary question. To assess evaluator reliability, we construct verification labels from presence/absence annotations and LLM-guided concept substitutions, and propose the Sensitivity-Invariance Ratio, which measures how selectively an evaluator responds to meaning-changing substitutions. Experiments show that concept-level scoring improves both question-answering and similarity-based evaluators, and MQAScore can be a more reliable and interpretable fine-grained complement to global similarity for evaluating text-to-music alignment.

title: Nitrogen vacancy cluster-mediated ferroelectric domain growth in wurtzite AlN
abstract: Aluminum nitride-based ferroelectrics combine high remanent polarization, thermal stability, weak size effects, a wide bandgap and back-end process compatibility, making them promising for high density non-volatile memory. However, their high coercive field ($E_\mathrm{c}$) and unclear polarization switching mechanism limit further applications. Theoretical predictions indicate preferential reversed domain growth along the polar axis, whereas experiments show nearly isotropic growth or preferential growth perpendicular to this axis. Here, we combine density functional theory, Deep Potential molecular dynamics and experimental characterization to determine how nitrogen vacancies ($V_\mathrm{N}$) regulate domain growth and $E_\mathrm{c}$. In ideal crystal, strong lattice coupling along the polar axis drives preferential domain growth in this direction. $V_\mathrm{N}$ locally weakens this coupling and promotes polarization nucleation. The spatial distribution of $V_\mathrm{N}$ and the temporal sequence of vacancy induced switching jointly determine the direction and morphology of reversed domain growth. We further show that scandium doping promotes $V_\mathrm{N}$ formation, thereby enhancing defect mediated nucleation and reducing $E_\mathrm{c}$. These findings establish a multiscale mechanism governing thin-film domain-growth kinetics and macroscopic $E_\mathrm{c}$, reconciling experimental observations with ideal crystal simulations and providing defect engineering principles for low-voltage, reliable and scalable ferroelectric devices.

title: Euler characteristic and flat cohomology of convex projective $4$-manifolds
abstract: Let $M=Ω/Γ$ be a closed properly convex real projective $4$-manifold. We prove the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture for this class of manifolds, i.e. $χ(M)\geq0$. The argument transfers Akagawa's double-form identity on the Cheng--Yau cone over $Ω$ to a Bochner identity on $M$, from which we deduce that $H^q(M;Λ^pE^*)=0$ whenever $q<p(n+1-p)/(n+1)$, in arbitrary dimension $n$, for some flat bundle $E$ naturally attached to $M$. In dimension four, this implies that the cohomology with coefficients in $Λ^2E^*$ concentrates in degree two.

title: Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms with dominated splitting Part 3: full formula with arbitrary multiplicities
abstract: We establish the full Ledrappier-Young entropy formula for ergodic invariant measures of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms when the positive Oseledets bundles and their nonpositive complement form a dominated splitting. We prove transverse formulas under three-block domination and equality of metric and unstable entropy under positive-nonpositive domination. To complete the proof, we develop a new mechanism for estimating partial entropy through comparisons of conditional information along orbits. Applications characterize vanishing transverse dimension, give upper pointwise dimension bounds and exact dimensionality of hyperbolic measures. In the quasi-isometric-center setting, this implies a $C^1$ invariance principle for measures with nonpositive center Lyapunov exponents.

title: I$^2$-KAN: Interpretable Intra- and Inter-Modal Multi-Pathway Representation Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to infer sentiment by integrating linguistic, acoustic, and visual information. However, many fusion methods integrate modality-specific representations and cross-modal interactions into joint representations, making it difficult to determine whether predictive utility arises from a modality itself or from its interactions with others. More fundamentally, a modality's standalone predictive utility may not faithfully reflect its interaction-conditioned predictive utility. To address this issue, we propose I$^2$-KAN, an interpretable multi-pathway framework that explicitly maintains intra-modal and pairwise inter-modal information in separate structural pathways. Each pathway is refined by a Task-Decoupled Linear-Gated Denoising Bottleneck (TDL-GDB) to learn compact and task-relevant representations, followed by structured Kolmogorov-Arnold Network fusion that retains explicit pathway associations and supports multi-level interpretation. Extensive experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS v2 demonstrate strong overall performance. Ablation and interpretability analyses consistently show across the three benchmarks that low standalone predictive utility does not necessarily imply low interaction-conditioned predictive utility: a modality that appears weak in isolation can remain informative through pairwise interactions. These findings highlight the interaction-dependent nature of multimodal utility and suggest that modality utility should be characterized from both standalone and interaction-conditioned perspectives.

title: A sharp isoperimetric bound for the ratio of the fifth and fourth eigenvalues of Dirichlet Laplacian
abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with $n\geq2$. The well-known Payne-Pólya-Weinberger conjecture for consecutive eigenvalue ratios asserts that $$ \frac{λ_{m+1}(Ω)}{λ_m(Ω)}\leq\left(\frac{j_{n / 2,1}}{j_{n / 2-1,1}}\right)^2,\quad m=1,2,3,\cdots. $$ Here, $j_{p,k}$ denotes the $k$-th positive zero of the Bessel function $J_p$, and $λ_j(Ω)$ are the Dirichlet eigenvalues of $Ω$, counted with multiplicity and ordered as $$ 0<λ_1(Ω)<λ_2(Ω)\leqλ_3(Ω)\leq\cdots. $$ The cases $m=1,2,3$ were established by Ashbaugh and Benguria in their seminal works. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the Payne-Pólya-Weinberger conjecture for $m=4$ by combining a quadratic-form identity with a Brouwer degree argument. We also extend the corresponding spectral inequality to arbitrary bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$.

title: Transformers with CoT Discover Heavy-Ball Acceleration Through Training
abstract: Modern transformers often solve complex tasks by generating and refining intermediate reasoning steps. To develop a theoretical understanding of chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, a notable recent study by Huang et al. (2025) viewed transformers as algorithm executors, and showed that when transformers' CoT steps are supervised by a gradient-descent teacher, they can learn to implement gradient descent for in-context weight prediction in linear regression. In this paper, we study the same in-context weight prediction task but ask whether CoT reasoning can go beyond merely imitating the teacher algorithm. We show that, after initial supervision from a gradient-descent teacher, further trajectory-level supervision using the true regression weights leads the model to implement the Heavy-Ball method, thereby achieving acceleration over the original teacher. Notably, this accelerated algorithm emerges without supervision from any Heavy-Ball teacher. Our results provide a concrete theoretical example in which transformer reasoning can discover new algorithms through training, rather than merely imitate the algorithm used for supervision.

title: What Pairwise Evaluation Misses: Reward Scores across Prompts
abstract: Reward models score responses for preference optimization, filtering and ranking, and pooling scores across prompts needs them to be comparable. Yet pairwise evaluation compares two responses to the same prompt, so any score component shared by a prompt's responses cancels and goes untested. We study this component by comparing between-prompt variation in model scores with the same variation in human ratings of the same responses. We propose a human-referenced audit, built from a between-prompt variance share, a sibling-rating regression and prompt substitutions, and apply it to eighteen released scorers and six matched training conditions. We find that scores cluster by prompt more than the ratings do: on HelpSteer2, six reward models have between-prompt shares of 0.34 to 0.64 against a human share near zero.
