abstract: We examine the use of neural networks in conjunction with the Born approximation for solving the inverse scattering problem for a penetrable medium in the frequency domain. The goal is a fast method for determining the refractive index of a scatterer from multistatic far-field measurements at one frequency. We present a new neural network model that seeks to improve on our previous results in by sharpening the reconstructed images. In addition, we present two other networks motivated by the corrected Born method that avoid the need to invert the regularized Born operator. These latter algorithms will be important for future three dimensional applications when the inverse Born approximation is difficult to compute, or when near-field measurements are used. Computational results illustrate that the new corrections to the Born approximation can provide an accurate and flexible approach to the inverse scattering problem.

title: Clean-label Poisoning Attack and Defense Game for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks
abstract: This paper studies interactions between clean-label poisoning attack and defense in vehicular networks using federated learning (FL). Basic Safety Message (BSM) classification for anomaly detection is modeled as a distributed learning problem over a vehicular network with dynamic topology. As a critical threat to FL, a feature-space clean-label attack is introduced, wherein benign samples are perturbed toward malicious feature extremes, degrading class separability while preserving labels. To counter this, a feature-consistency relabeling defense is proposed to detect and relabel suspicious samples. A game-theoretic framework is developed to capture attack-defense interactions and characterize equilibrium strategies based on attack effectiveness and cost parameters. Results show that the attack scales effectively with compromised nodes, while the proposed defense keeps attack success low without degrading clean accuracy and shifts equilibrium regions toward attack-averse regimes.

title: Floquet Engineering of Momentum Gaps in Magnonic Time Crystals: Slow-Drive Amplification and In-Gap Propagation
abstract: Photonic time crystals host momentum gaps in which waves grow exponentially but cannot propagate. We establish their magnonic counterpart in a thin film with periodically switched anisotropy, deriving its Floquet band structure and confirming it micromagnetically. Gaps require a precession-ellipticity contrast. The waveform controls high-order gaps: a single 1~GHz switching drive amplifies a comb of spin-wave bands, from 2.5 to 4.5~GHz, above Gilbert losses even with smoothed edges, unlike sinusoidal modulation. With the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction, amplified packets propagate inside the gap while growing.

title: Majorana Edge-to-bound State Transition in Interferometric Superconductor Rings
abstract: Manipulating flux quanta in topological superconductors is central to vortex braiding in quantum computing. Their interferometric superconducting rings can host either topologically protected edge states with fluxes confined inside the central hollow area or vortex bound states in flux cores at the annulus walls. Here we demonstrate a strategy to drive topological edge states into vortex bound states by tuning the relative scale of vortex size and annulus width in nano-ring interferometric device on 2M-WS$_2$ topological superconductor. Near its superconducting transition where the coherence length exceeds the annulus width, Little-Parks oscillations exhibit expected periods for flux bundles in ring-center, consistent with edge states residing at inner and outer rims of the annulus. Upon cooling, where the coherence length shrinks below the annulus width, the unexpectedly increased oscillation period reflects multiple fluxes distributed along annulus region in flux necklace configuration, implying a transition from extended edge states to localized vortex bound states. Ginzburg-Landau simulations and local density-of-states calculations with Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations reveal that large values for both Ginzburg-Landau parameter and flux-pinning energy are vital for such a transition. Our findings provide a novel strategy for understanding flux manipulation towards flux braiding and topological quantum computing.

title: SCDM-HTD: Spectral-Wise Conditional Diffusion Model for Hyperspectral Target Detection
abstract: Hyperspectral target detection (HTD) aims to locate and recognize objects at a fine-grained scale, playing a pivotal role in remote sensing. Despite significant progress, current HTD methods primarily focus on feature comparison while neglecting distribution learning for background-target separation, which can limit detection robustness in practical applications. This paper addresses this issue by introducing a spectral-wise conditional diffusion model that reformulates HTD as a task of generating a detection map. Specifically, we treat background and target confidence scores as training samples and use the corresponding pixel spectra as guiding conditions to capture the distributional discrepancy between background and target through diffusion and denoising. To enhance practical applicability, we propose a lightweight conditional denoising network based on multilayer perceptron to map noisy confidence scores to their ideal counterparts and adopt a deterministic reverse non-Markov chain to skip sampling steps, thereby accelerating the generation process. Furthermore, we introduce a composite loss to improve background-target separation. This loss integrates constrained energy minimization loss to enhance target saliency and suppress the background by maximizing the target response while minimizing average output energy, alongside binary cross-entropy loss to classify background and target using pixel-wise labels. Experimental results on four benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, with improvements in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visual effects.

title: Rational $S$-functions for second order ODEs with non-Liouvillian first integrals
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
abstract: The $S$-function method for rational second order ODEs $y''=φ(x,y,y')$ uses $S=I_y/I_z$, attached to a first integral $I$, which satisfies a Riccati equation along the flow; it was designed for Liouvillian $I$. We study the case of rational $S$ with non-Liouvillian $I$. From any rational $g(x,y,z)$ with $g_z\neq0$ and any linear equation $A_2w''+A_1w'+A_0w=0$ with polynomial coefficients, the substitution $w'/w=g(x,y,y')$ yields a rational 2ODE whose first integral is built from two independent solutions, and $S=g_y/g_z$: the Wronskian cancels, so $S$ does not see the linear equation, and one rational $S$ is shared by equations with and without Liouvillian first integrals. Conversely, given $(φ,S)$, membership in this class reduces to a rational first integral of an explicit planar vector field plus a Möbius-invariant Riccati test in $x$, which recovers the linear equation. A transfer theorem shows that $I$ is Liouvillian if and only if this equation has a Liouvillian solution, so Liouvillianity is decidable on the class by Kovacic's algorithm: a three-variable problem with no a priori degree bound is reduced to two classical ones. On nine pull-back equations of degree up to $15$, given without information on their construction, the procedure recovers the Airy equation and the Bessel equation of order zero.

title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
abstract: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.

title: Veering triangulations of once-punctured torus bundles are unique
abstract: We show that each hyperbolic once-punctured torus bundle has exactly one veering triangulation. We also find manifolds for which the exact number of veering structures is known and is greater than one. Finally, we give new examples of manifolds without veering triangulations.

title: Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment with Reward-Model Gradients
abstract: GRPO shares a response-level advantage across tokens, leaving unresolved how strongly each token should contribute to learning. Updates induced by the shared advantage reinforce or suppress the sampled token at each position, but these updates do not always point toward increasing reward at the token level. This motivates a work-based view of credit: just as work depends on the component of force along a displacement, token credit should reflect the local reward change along the policy update direction. We introduce Direction-Aware Token Credit Assignment (DATC), which maps frozen reward-model gradients into policy logit space and allocates weights by evaluating the alignment between the reward direction and GRPO's signed sampled-action update direction, while preserving the sign and mean of the response-level advantage. DATC outperforms GRPO in all four settings across two model families.

title: The Evolution of Self-Gravitating Radiating Geodesic Fluid Spheres Instantaneously Admitting a Time-Like Killing
abstract: In this study we analyze the effects produced by the sudden appearance of a time-like Killing vector (TKV), on the evolution of radiating geodesic fluids. This is achieved by resorting to the concept of asymmetry factor which allows the instantaneous appearance of a given symmetry for a given value of the time-like coordinate. All relevant physical variables are analyzed in detail showing the imprints of the emergence of TKV at some point of the evolution. The main lesson that can be extracted from the obtained results is that the sudden appearance of a TKV, even for an infinitesimal period of time, drastically changes the subsequent evolution of the system. Of particular relevance is the appearance of a thermal effect linking the asymmetry factor and the relaxation time. The potential applications of these results, on the study of gravitational collapse, are discussed at the end of the paper.

title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of HER2 Status from Whole-Brain MRI in Breast Cancer Brain Metastases
abstract: Purpose: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status is a key biomarker relevant for prognostication and treatment decision making in metastatic breast cancer. Thus, the aim of this work was to explore whether HER2 status can be predicted directly from whole-brain post-contrast T1-weighted (T1w) MRI scans in breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM) using deep learning, and whether providing explicit tumour segmentation information improves prediction. Methods: Using the publicly available BCBM-Radiogenomics dataset, we analysed 135 patients, including 70 HER2+ and 65 HER2- patients. Three approaches were implemented and evaluated: a conventional radiomics model, a simple fully convolutional network (SFCN) using T1w MRI scans alone, and an SFCN using T1w MRI scans with an expert-derived tumour mask as an additional input channel. Results: The radiomics model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.602 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.528--0.677) while the SFCN achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.667 (95% CI, 0.63--0.71) using T1w MRI scans alone, which increased to 0.692 (95% CI, 0.58--0.81) when an explicit tumour mask was additionally provided. Conclusion: However, the modest performance across all approaches demonstrates the difficulty of predicting HER2 status from structural MRI scans alone. The difference between the segmentation-free and mask-guided SFCN models suggests that much of the predictive signal captured by the deep-learning model may be learned directly from whole-brain T1w MRI without requiring explicit tumour delineation. These findings support further investigation of segmentation-free deep-learning approaches as a potential non-invasive strategy to support HER2 status determination in BCBM.

title: Large profinite genus and extensions in Bestvina-Brady groups
abstract: We construct the first examples of uncountable families of residually finite duality groups of type $FP$, all of which have isomorphic profinite completions, while being pairwise not quasi-isometric. To establish these finiteness properties, we prove conjectures of Leary regarding groups of deck transformations of certain cubical branched covers being residually finite and virtually special. The main new tool is a strong separability result for Bestvina-Brady groups, allowing the extension of any finite quotient of many Bestvina-Brady subgroups to a finite quotient of the whole group. This gives a finite version of the congruence extension property, which we also establish for the same group pairs.

title: Predictive Long-Horizon Progress Modeling with Action-Aware Quantification
abstract: Quantitative and dense task progress feedback is essential for robotic manipulation across data curation, policy evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Existing progress annotations often rely on sparse keyframe markings derived from subjective manual judgments, limiting their scalability and cross-task consistency, particularly in long-horizon manipulation. To overcome these challenges, we propose action-aware quantification, a unified progress specification that decomposes long-horizon trajectories into object-level subtasks via a vision-language model (VLM) and assigns weighted action credits to capture fine-grained execution dynamics. Using VLM auto-labeling and human calibration, we construct an 800+ hour training video dataset and LOOM, a long-horizon progress benchmark containing 19,618 human-calibrated evaluation frames. To model these dense progress dynamics, we introduce NimCritic, a predictive progress critic trained via Joint Video-Progress Learning. We further incorporate Historical Progress Perturbation to mitigate sequential drift, and design a contrastive Video-Progress Alignment objective that bridges asymmetric expert streams by mutually grounding intermediate visual dynamics and denoised progress trajectories. NimCritic matches or outperforms state-of-the-art process reward models (PRMs) on the established Video Progress Benchmark (VPB) and LOOM, surpassing GVL (GPT-6-Sol) on VPB by about 65% in terminal success accuracy (TSA). On the large-scale RoboArena policy evaluation benchmark, it also retrieves human-selected successful rollouts with about 97% overall recall. These results establish action-aware quantification as a scalable foundation for dense progress feedback in robotic manipulation.

title: Resampling-Based Inference for Incomplete Paired Functional Data
abstract: We consider testing equality of mean functions for paired functional data, where one entire function is missing. To use all available information from the paired and unpaired observations, we propose globalized test statistics that are based on a weighted sum of point-wise paired-$t$ and Welch-$t$-type statistics. By the use of empirical process theory, we derive the asymptotic limit distributions of the resulting test statistics under the null hypothesis and show consistency against fixed alternatives. As they are non-pivotal and contain complex dependencies from the paired and incomplete observations, a permutation and parametric bootstrap procedures is proposed to compute critical values. The work includes a theoretical investigation of the asymptotic behaviour of the two resampling approaches and state regularity conditions under which the corresponding resampling tests are valid. Simulation studies show that the proposed methods provide accurate type I error control and competitive power for most settings under study. An illustrative analysis of functional emission data demonstrates the applicability of the methods.

title: Density control of large-scale multi-agent systems via tuning of agent interactions
abstract: Collective behavior in biological systems emerges through adaptive interactions among units, enabling large populations to coordinate without centralized control. This mechanism raises the question of whether collective behavior in engineered multi-agent systems can likewise be regulated by modifying the interaction law between agents, rather than by directly controlling individual units. To answer this question, we consider large-scale multi-agent systems evolving on a ring and treat the interaction kernel as a time-varying control variable whose evolution regulates the collective dynamics. Using a mean-field formulation, we develop a framework for the analysis and design of kernel-based controllers. We derive explicit conditions for controllability in application-relevant scenarios, and synthesize a state-feedback controller to regulate the kernel dynamics, validated on the microscopic, discrete dynamics. Numerical simulations demonstrate the approach's effectiveness and robustness to unmodeled perturbations. This work constitutes a first step in the design of bio-inspired control strategies for large-scale multi-agent systems by modulation of interactions between agents.

title: Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19
abstract: Interleukin-23 (IL-23) drives T-helper-17 inflammation underlying inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis; anti-p19 antibodies are clinically effective but large, costly, and injectable. De novo miniproteins are an attractive alternative, yet published designs target the IL-23 receptor; the IL-23 cytokine itself has not been addressed. A further obstacle is that the standard confidence score (ipTM) tracks construct length rather than interface quality. We computationally design miniprotein binders against the IL-23R-binding face of p19 (PDB 3DUH) and score every design with ipSAE, a length-robust interface metric derived from AlphaFold-initial-guess predicted aligned error. A conventional RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/ColabFold pipeline yields no reliable predicted interface across 972 designs (best ipSAE 0.30), and a scoring artifact, in which single-sequence ColabFold under-rates binder pLDDT by approximately 56 points, explains an earlier misleading "binders do not fold" signal. An interface-optimized hallucination method (BindCraft), scored identically, yields 42 of 50 designs above ipSAE 0.60 (best 0.804). An AlphaFold-independent geometric check reproduces the conventional failure: no top-ranked conventional design reaches the buried area or interface hydrogen-bond count of the weakest lead. Five all-alpha-helical leads (72-104 residues) collectively engage all six targeted hotspots; two dock within the intact p40/p19 heterodimer and all show favorable Rosetta energetics. A p40-alone counter-screen returns ipSAE 0.00 for all five, indicating no spurious p40 interface. To our knowledge, these are the first computationally proposed de novo miniprotein candidates designed to occlude the IL-23R-binding face of IL-23 p19. All results require experimental validation.

title: AI Alignment for Digital Democracy: Fairer Voters Representation against LLM Biases
abstract: AI representation is emerging in digital democracy, assisting in voter emulation and decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) behave differently depending on the model, the prompt context, and the voter information they receive, representing some groups more accurately than others and potentially making the emulation unfair to certain groups. We investigate demographic biases in LLM-emulated electorates: how accurately LLMs represent individual votes, whether some voter groups are represented more accurately than others, and whether AI alignment can reduce these disparities without sacrificing overall accuracy. Using three U.S. presidential elections, we compare a closed-source and an open-source LLM across voters' demographic features and test AI alignment strategies toward fairer voter representation. Removing gender from the voter profile reduces the largest group error of the models by 22-42%, and removing education reduces it by 64%, whereas removing self-reported race increases the mean group error by over 40%, all without lowering accuracy. Common alignment strategies, such as repeated queries or fairness instructions, do not reduce these errors and can double them.

title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents
abstract: Hospitals regularly buy software that clinicians and patients depend on. Because these purchases are costly, hard to reverse and can affect patient care, buyers look for evidence of which peer institutions already use a product and which systems it connects to. This evidence is public but scattered across vendor websites, press releases and third-party pages. Language-model agents can now collect it at low cost, but the correctness of the extracted claims is difficult to establish, and a wrongly listed customer can mislead buyers and misrepresent an organisation. We present a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph of customer and integration relations from the open web under one rule: every edge must be supported by a verbatim quote from its source page. Pages come from a deterministic crawl of each vendor's site and a budgeted ReAct agent that searches the rest of the web. A permissive extractor proposes relations with quotes, and a layered grounding stage decides which to keep, using a referent step that reads the whole page when a quote names only one side, deterministic checks, and a panel of five model calls voting on nine criteria. On 61 vendors, the pipeline reaches 0.94 precision and 0.71 recall against a page-level key covering the 6,428 candidate relations proposed by its extractor, whose verdicts were drafted by one model and re-checked with a second. Against the golden reference, the marketplace's own curated list, it scores lower, but 89% of the relations it keeps that the reference lacks are stated on a page. A confidence score built from the panel's votes keeps more correct relations than the fixed rule at the same precision, and reaches 0.90 precision at 0.90 recall. We also discuss how narrow, bounded model calls, string-matched evidence and voting address long-context degradation and run-to-run variance.

title: On quasi-Albanese morphisms for log canonical Calabi-Yau pairs II
abstract: Centering on quasi-Albanese morphisms, we prove several structural theorems for Calabi-Yau pairs.

title: Bounding single-copy information causality violations
abstract: Information causality is a physical principle that constrains bipartite post-quantum nonlocal correlations from information-theoretic assumptions. A direct characterization of the correlations satisfying it, however, remains difficult because the defining entropic condition must hold for all admissible protocols in the corresponding task. Here, we formulate the single-copy information causality problem as an optimization over all protocol parameters and simplify it by proving a deterministic reduction. We then show that generic adaptive multi-copy protocols can be represented as single-copy protocols applied to an effective behavior obtained by local wirings. As a consequence, for families of correlations closed under wirings, excluding single-copy violations suffices to exclude all finite-copy adaptive-protocol violations. We formulate the resulting membership and set-inclusion problems as optimization problems and discuss possible semidefinite programming relaxations. As an application, we study expansions of the information causality functional around zero-capacity channels, generalizing a method recently employed by Gachechiladze and Miklin to derive the Tsirelson--Landau--Masanes boundary from information causality. For expansions centered on channels whose output distribution has full support, imposing the second-order constraints for all single-copy protocols characterizes exactly the set of macroscopic locality in the CHSH scenario. Expanding instead around appropriate constant-output channels with perturbations that change the channel support, we show that every single-copy IC violation can be witnessed already at first order with a channel of arbitrarily small capacity.

title: Video-MemComp: Taylor-Guided Sensitivity-Aware Memory Management for Streaming Video Understanding
abstract: The rapid growth of video data has created an urgent need for efficient video understanding systems that can handle long and continuous visual inputs, posing significant challenges for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) due to severe memory bottlenecks. Moreover, existing compression methods often overlook the explosive accumulation of approximation errors. To address this issue, we propose Video-MemComp, a training-free and sensitivity-aware context management framework for memory-constrained streaming video understanding. Our method theoretically decomposes compression error into orthogonal local approximation error and layer-wise structural sensitivity via a first-order Taylor expansion. To minimize local approximation error, we perform token aggregation in a pre-RoPE safe zone with an attention-conserving logit bias, mitigating geometric distortions caused by RoPE rotations. To manage layer-wise structural sensitivity, we dynamically allocate the KV cache budget based on offline gradient priors and online context entropy, prioritizing high-sensitivity layers. Video-MemComp outperforms or achieves performance comparable to full-cache and state-of-the-art compression methods on benchmarks including MLVU, VideoMME, and EgoSchema. Notably, it improves the overall accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-3B from 62.3% to 64.1% while reducing the KV cache to an equivalent of 6,000 tokens per layer, saving over 90% of KV memory.

title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Timely state updates are essential for coordination and monitoring in multi-agent systems, such as teams of mobile robots exchanging state information. When agents share a wireless channel, collisions and slow convergence of distributed access schemes can degrade information freshness over finite operating periods. This paper proposes age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), a distributed medium access control protocol for minimizing age of information (AoI). Once its age reaches a threshold, an agent starts a local frame with a mandatory transmission and, if unsuccessful, makes one further attempt at a uniformly selected remaining slot. Each attempt carries a freshly generated update. AFRA requires only local state and acknowledgment feedback, with shared slot boundaries but independently timed local frames. We prove almost-sure convergence from any legal initial state to collision-free periodic operation when the frame length $L$ and age threshold $T$ satisfy $L\ge T>N\ge2$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We also derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average AoI, and average peak AoI. Simulations demonstrate that AFRA combines rapid convergence at small age thresholds with lower window-averaged AoI than the existing age-aware random access schemes evaluated in this study.

title: Probing the star-forming environment of GRB across cosmic ages with high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy: From \textit{XMM-Newton}/RGS and \textit{XRISM}/Resolve to \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU
abstract: Optical and infrared GRB absorption spectroscopy provides valuable insight into host-galaxy properties across cosmic time. However, the star-forming region embedding the progenitor, on scales $\lesssim 100~\mathrm{pc}$ is heavily ionized by the GRB emission, making X-ray spectroscopy the sole probe of its physical and chemical conditions. We characterize the GRB-embedding medium as a function of progenitor type and cosmic epoch via high-resolution X-ray spectroscopy. We extend our study to high-redshift GRBs to evaluate how effectively X-ray absorption signatures can distinguish between pristine, Pop~III-, and Pop~II-enriched environments. Using the time-dependent photoionization code \texttt{TEPID}, we self-consistently calculate the ionization structure of the absorber, the energies and the strengths of the resulting absorption lines. We analyze a flux-selected sample of GRBs showing strong evidence for time-dependent photoionization, and search for predicted narrow features in the RGS spectra. We also assess the performance of \textit{XRISM}/Resolve and \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU in detecting these features. In the single archival case with sufficient RGS signal-to-noise ratio (GRB~090618 at $z=0.54$), we find $\approx 3σ$ combined evidence for narrow, highly ionized Fe~L absorption lines. For bright nearby GRBs, \textit{XRISM}/Resolve can detect Fe~K absorption lines even in its current gate-valve-closed configuration ($\sim 3$ expected events/yr). \textit{NewAthena}/X-IFU will enable systematic population studies of GRB environments, delivering redshifts with precision comparable to optical/IR spectroscopy, unaffected by dust obscuration and Ly-$α$ forest absorption. Crucially, it will precisely diagnose the density, size, metallicity, and abundance patterns, ultimately revealing whether high-$z$ GRBs originate in pristine, Pop~III-, or Pop~II-enriched media.

title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
abstract: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.

title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
abstract: Large language models are trained to predict tokens from a finite vocabulary, each represented by a vector in a $d$-dimensional embedding space. Therefore, token prediction is a classification problem whose classes have a geometry determined by the embedding. We study how this geometry affects learning in a minimal solvable model: a linear predictor that maps a sequence of $N$ embedded tokens to a $d$-dimensional output through one $d\times d$ matrix per position, trained in the teacher--student setting. We call this the \textit{token perceptron}. We compute its generalization error with the replica method, taking $N\to\infty$ at fixed number of examples per position $α=P/N$ and keeping $d$ and the vocabulary size $D$ finite. As a first reference case, we consider continuous embeddings on the sphere, which isolate the role of the embedding dimension. The natural load is then $α/d$, and for $d>1$ a normalized label fixes the direction of the teacher output, so the problem becomes a noiseless regression: the teacher is recovered exactly above $α_{\rm rec}=d^2/(d-1)$, and spherical cross-entropy reaches this threshold at large inverse temperature. In the same setting the storage capacity of random associations scales as $d^2$ for margins $O(1/\sqrt{d})$. We then turn to vocabulary embeddings, where a label only identifies the Voronoi cell of the teacher output, so that each example imposes inequalities rather than equations, as in the classical perceptron. We compute the Bayes-optimal error for a given embedding matrix through an approximate spectral closure and show that the optimal learner first resolves the directions in which the vocabulary has the largest variance, even when the teacher is isotropic.

title: Triangle-Free Sets in Exact-Distance Hamming Graphs
abstract: Let $T_q(n,r)$ be the largest size of a vertex set inducing a triangle-free subgraph of the graph on $[q]^n$ whose edges join words at Hamming distance $r$. We study this quantity for fixed alphabet size and fixed distance, with particular emphasis on the ternary cube. Alphabet restriction transfers the binary fixed-distance theorem of Balogh, Chen, and Li to give $T_q(n,2h)=O_h(q^n/n^h)$. We extend the known distance-one formula and distance-two order to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, obtaining $T_q(n,1)=2q^{n-1}$ and $T_q(n,2)=Θ_q(q^n/n)$, and establish $T_3(n,4)=Θ(3^n/n^2)$. For general fixed distance, we prove \[ T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}\!\left( \frac{q^n\sqrt{\log n}}{n^{(r+\lfloor r/2\rfloor)/2}} \right)\qquad(q\ge3), \] while we show that $T_q(n,r)=Ω_{q,r}(q^n/n^{\lfloor(q-1)r/q\rfloor})$ holds for prime-power $q$ and $r\ge2$ via the extended BCH parity-check constructions. At distance three, we construct coordinate weights avoiding bounded-coefficient three-term relations and obtain \[ T_q(n,3)\ge q^n/[n\exp(O_q(\sqrt{\log n}))]. \] Our main ternary construction combines cap partitions, multicolor triangle Ramsey colorings, and a quadratic map to obtain \[ T_3(n,3)=Ω\!\left( \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\,3^n\right). \] A coordinate-line counting argument gives the complementary upper bound $T_3(n,3)\le(5/27+O(n^{-1}))3^n$, together with an explicit bound for every fixed $q\ge3$. Whether the ternary density tends to zero remains open.

title: Robustness of the scaled transverse-momentum correlator and the contribution of meson--baryon fluctuations at RHIC energies
abstract: The search for the QCD critical point relies on identifying non-monotonic signatures in event-by-event fluctuation observables, such as the scaled two-particle transverse-momentum correlator $C_{p_T}$. Using a microscopic transport model (UrQMD), we establish the robustness of $C_{p_T}$ against the variations that distinguish the datasets in the relevant collision energy regime, namely the choice of centrality estimator, finite tracking efficiency, and acceptance, including the difference between collider and fixed-target running. In addition, it has recently been proposed, based on UrQMD yields, that the measured non-monotonicity requires no critical dynamics and instead follows from the event-by-event composition of the final state. We show that this contribution is governed by event-by-event fluctuations in the meson-baryon composition, rather than by the mean yields alone. Using the composition fluctuations obtained from UrQMD, we find that the minimum in the two-component calculation disappears.

title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
abstract: We derive a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory for the metastable heterogeneous G state reported in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central result is that type-II-like mixed-state physics can emerge structurally with the random internal stress field playing the role of the magnetic field. Frozen eigenstrain due to elastic incompatibility between ordered cores and the amorphous matrix generates incompatible stress, while the non-affine internal strain in the liquid-like matrix in between the ordered cores relaxes that stress over a finite screening length $λ_σ$ (analogous to the London length in the superconducting problem). Structural order heals over a distinct mechanically-dressed length $ξ_G$; their ratio $κ_G=λ_σ/ξ_G$ provides the structural counterpart of the Ginzburg-Landau parameter. Because the matrix is transiently rigid yet locally relaxational only over an intermediate time window, the same mechanism selects crystal for slow protocols, a heterogeneous G state at intermediate rates, and a homogeneous L-like glass under rapid arrest. Residual incompatibility frustrates coarsening, allowing finite ordered cores and screened, orientation-dependent core interactions. The resulting texture is an inverted Abrikosov analogue: structural order resides in the cores, whereas incompatible-stress screening is carried by the surrounding disordered matrix. The theory yields direct simulation and experimental tests through stress-decay, structural-healing, non-affine-susceptibility, and kinetic measurements.

title: SREdit: Scene Response Guided Appearance Editing for Projection Mapping
abstract: Projection-based appearance editing changes selected visual attributes of a physical object through projection mapping (PM). To display a desired appearance, PM typically uses projector compensation, which computes a projector input that counteracts the geometric and photometric distortions of the scene. Compensation can only approximate this appearance within the available projection range, and it cannot revise the appearance itself. Pretrained LLM-based image editors provide a direct way to produce the desired appearance from a text prompt or reference image; projector compensation can then attempt to reproduce the edited result through projection. However, these editors do not have an accurate measure of the scene geometry or scene response. Therefore, their outputs may contain geometric misalignment, inconsistent shading, or changes outside the available projection range, which downstream projector compensation cannot correct. To address this problem, we introduce SREdit, an efficient response-guided framework for projection-based appearance editing. SREdit estimates a scene response map from the reconstructed scene that reflects how strongly projected illumination can affect different surface regions. SREdit uses the source appearance to constrain the early sampling process and preserve registration with the fixed physical object, while the scene response map adapts the amount of editing across surface regions. Experiments across two pretrained image editors show that SREdit improves projected appearance quality and reproduction fidelity. It adds less than one second per image with negligible VRAM overhead. Participants also consistently preferred the results produced with SREdit in our user study.

title: Capacity Modification for Matching with Couples: An Integer Programming and Computational Study
abstract: We study capacity modification in the Hospitals/Residents problem with Couples, in which hospital capacities and a stable matching are jointly determined. Exact and Cutoff integer programming formulations are developed for the resulting problem. We assume that, for each couple, either both members are matched or neither is. For arbitrary strict preferences, every instance admits a stable matching after changing each hospital capacity by at most two. Total capacity increases by at most one, and this bound is tight. Under sub-responsive and sub-complete couple preferences, a stable matching exists after adding at most one position to each hospital. The total number of additions is at most the number of couples, and this bound is also tight. Computational experiments show that Exact formulations are modestly faster at fixed capacities, whereas Cutoff formulations perform substantially better in the minimum repair experiments and attain higher completion rates in markets with up to 30,000 doctors. Across 96,000 synthetic and reconstructed markets, small capacity changes restore existence whenever no stable matching exists at the original capacities.

title: Consommé: Conditioned Token Merging for Split Inference
abstract: Split inference partitions a Vision Transformer between a resource-constrained edge device and a server. However, transmitting intermediate tokens across the communication channel is costly. Deploying fine-tuned backbones to every endpoint becomes expensive as well. We study token reduction for split inference under a frozen backbone, where only a small adapter is shipped. We observe that the CLS token plays a dual role: it acts as the global summary the receiver needs for classification, and it serves as a signal on which patches to keep. We propose Consommé, a method utilizing both characteristics. There, an information bottleneck compresses the CLS token into a compact latent which is transmitted in place of the full CLS token and conditions a learned patch gate merging patches into exactly $k$ tokens via soft assignment. It reaches any budget in a single step, thus escaping the per-layer cap of bipartite matching (BPM). On DeiT-S/T, it leads all methods at aggressive token budgets and remains operable at shallow splits where BPM cannot operate, while matching fine-tuned methods at gentle budgets at a fraction of their deployment cost.

title: A Compact Single-Beam Optically Pumped Magnetometer Based on Absorption Detection
abstract: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.

title: ParaTaxe: a Suite of Tools for Processing and Publishing Multi-parallel Corpora
abstract: Over the past fifteen years, digital tools for parallelizing and aligning textual corpora have developed significantly within the field of digital humanities. Several projects and software tools have been created to compare different translations or versions of texts. Despite these technical advances, many parallel corpora produced in academic contexts quickly become inaccessible online due to the lack of maintenance or funding. To address this gap, we present a suite of open-source tools developed within the ACR Grimm Tradalign and ParaTaxe projects. This suite includes the AIlign aligner, based on multilingual embeddings, a Python processing pipeline for converting and aligning corpora, a web interface called ParaTaxe for managing collections of parallel corpora, and a web interface for exploring aligned corpora built with TEI-Publisher.

title: Unconventional charge density wave order in ErTe$_{3}$: symmetry breakings and fluctuations probed by Raman scattering
abstract: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.

title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by Hörsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of Hörsch et al.

title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning
abstract: Replay-based Continual Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by keeping a buffer of past samples, making buffer composition critical under a fixed memory budget. Recent coreset-based replay methods improve buffer quality using model-derived gradients, losses, or auxiliary optimization, but incur substantial computational overhead as memory is repeatedly updated. We propose CARES, a continual model-optimization-free approach for buffer construction that instead exploits the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space using class-aware, density-weighted coverage. We evaluate CARES across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings. On Tiny-ImageNet, CARES is 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than existing coreset-based selectors. Although CARES achieves this speedup using no training signal from the continual learner, it ranks among the state of the art across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 7.58 percentage points under class imbalance while also attaining higher average accuracy on Tiny-ImageNet. Code will be released upon publication

title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Real-world 3D reconstruction pipelines often rely on multi-view images degraded by lossy compression. While compression artifacts have been extensively studied in single-image or video restoration, their impact on multi-view geometry remains largely overlooked. In this work, we identify compression-induced cross-view geometric inconsistency as a critical failure mode, where view-dependent artifacts disrupt feature matching, dense correspondence, camera parameter estimation, and downstream 3D reconstruction tasks such as novel view synthesis. To address this problem, we propose CompMVR, a compression-aware multi-view diffusion restoration framework that jointly refines compressed views while preserving cross-view consistency, and construct compressed datasets for systematic evaluation. Unlike conventional restoration methods that optimize each image independently for 2D perceptual quality, CompMVR leverages learned compression priors and cross-view correspondence to recover visual details while improving geometric reliability across views. Experiments across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels demonstrate gains in restoration quality and downstream 3D tasks, including novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching. These results establish compressed multi-view restoration as a distinct problem and highlight its importance for 3D reconstruction under lossy compression. Code and data for this paper are available at https://mchaewon.github.io/CompMVR-project-page/.

title: Multiplicative vs. Additive State Coupling in Learned Optimizer Schedules
abstract: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.

title: Frontier-OPD: Discovering the Edge of Agent Capability and Teaching Agents to Go Beyond
abstract: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.

title: Quantum Cadence: Post-Quantum Consensus with Multiple Concurrent Proposers
abstract: The consensus protocols of most high-performance blockchains use quorum certificates, which bundle the signatures of a quorum of validators. Signature schemes such as BLS can aggregate the signatures of a whole quorum into a single short signature, which keeps these certificates small. A large-scale quantum computer would break these schemes, and no post-quantum scheme with comparable aggregate size and aggregation time is known. Without aggregation, a certificate holds one large post-quantum signature per member of the quorum, so it becomes infeasible for each validator to broadcast certificates, as modern consensus protocols often require. We present Quantum Cadence, a post-quantum consensus protocol with multiple concurrent proposers that avoids certificates altogether: every validator counts quorums among the messages it has received itself. Its safety and liveness do not even depend on signatures, although we add signatures to obtain accountability. Quantum Cadence builds on Cadence and replaces its slot consensus, Chorus, with Quantum Chorus, which keeps the optimal fast-path latency of Chorus: dissemination followed by two rounds of votes. When its fast path fails, Quantum Chorus runs Coda, our signature-free Byzantine agreement for multiple proposers. We also outline how the Conductor, which schedules the slots of Cadence, can be adapted to Quantum Cadence. In simulations with 200 validators, Quantum Chorus has a latency comparable to that of Chorus and scales better with the number of proposers.

title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by a thin truss
abstract: We consider the homogenization problem of the stationary Stokes equations in a periodically perforated domain whose solid structure consists of a thin truss. That is, the width $a_ε$ of the truss tends to zero faster than the period size $ε$. We identify the different scaling regimes and derive the corresponding effective equations. In the critical regime, we obtain the Brinkman equations, while in the subcritical regime, we recover the unchanged Stokes equations. In a subrange of the supercritical regime, we derive Darcy's law as the effective equation. Furthermore, we explicitly compute the effective coefficients in the Darcy and Brinkman limits. Moreover, as a tool in the analysis, we establish the analogous homogenization result for a periodic forest of cylinders. Finally, we also consider the homogenization result for a fence of cylinders.

title: Choosing What to Observe: Higher-Order Obstructions in Horn Abduction
abstract: An explanation may exist in every complete context yet be impossible to select from the information observed. We study this distinction in finite propositional Horn abduction with integrity constraints. Observations are sufficient when each report admits one hypothesis set that is consistent and entails the manifestation in every compatible context. We characterize sufficiency by minimal context families with no common explanation. Their variable spans form a canonical hypergraph whose transversals are exactly the sufficient observation sets. The characterization recovers classical discernibility for unique explanations and supports composition across independent components. Minimal obstructions have unbounded cardinality even for acyclic rules, while rectangular explanation families admit a tight bound given by their largest choice domain. With circuit-defined contexts, sufficiency is $Π_3^P$-complete and selecting at most $k$ observable variables is $Σ_4^P$-complete, already for unrestricted contexts and acyclic rules. The selection reduction makes observation choices enforce globally fixed existential commitments. Explicit contexts reduce both tasks to NP-complete problems; tabulated explanation families make sufficiency polynomial. These results connect explanatory choice, information requirements, and representation cost.

title: Low-Crossing Spanning Paths via Quasi-Uniform Sampling and their Applications
abstract: Given a set system (X, S), we consider the problems of constructing perfect matchings and spanning paths (also known as Welzl orders) of X with low crossing numbers with respect to S. Matchings with low crossing numbers were originally introduced in the late 1980s in the seminal works of Welzl [29, 30] and Chazelle-Welzl [7], who showed that any set system (X, S) with bounded dual VC-dimension d has a matching with crossing number O |X| 1-1/d , which is optimal. Low-crossing matchings and spanning paths have found several applications outside of their initial realm of computational geometry, including algorithmic graph theory, model checking, and game theory. In many of these applications, |S| is near-linear in |X|, which motivated the search for an improved construction for this regime. However, the proposed new algorithms provided only average-case bounds or sub-optimal crossing number guarantees for d $\ge$ 2 [5, 12]. We propose a new quasi-uniform sampling based framework. This allows us to obtain a simple algorithm with expected running time of __ |X| 2 + |S| $\bullet$ |X| , which improves upon the previous-best Our result has several immediate consequences, including new faster algorithms for constructing low-crossing spanning paths for set systems induced by balls, as well as for neighborhood set systems of graphs. Moreover, we get the first quadratic-time algorithm for combinatorial discrepancy, with nearly optimal discrepancy (up to a log factor), for bounded dual VC-dimension set systems. Beyond these applications, we believe that our idea could be applied to other algorithms that use the multiplicative weight update method.

title: Beam Search for Error-Correcting Codes via Conditional Diffusion
abstract: We introduce a diffusion framework for neural decoding of error-correcting codes (ECCs). We interpret decoding as a conditional diffusion process that progressively predicts codeword bits while treating the physical channel observation as fixed side information. At each stage, a neural model estimates bitwise posteriors conditioned on the physical observation and the current noisy state of the codeword. We focus particularly on masked diffusion, for which the reverse process naturally induces a Maxwell beam search (MBS) procedure inspired by the Maxwell construction of Measson et al. Rather than committing to a single uncertain decision, the decoder maintains multiple candidate trajectories, removes parity-infeasible candidates, and ranks the remaining candidates using accumulated reverse-transition log-probabilities. We evaluate the framework across multiple code families on binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN). Experiments show competitive decoding performance across Polar, low-density parity-check (LDPC), and Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem (BCH) codes. The MBS decoder consistently improves upon the corresponding single-trajectory diffusion decoder and, in all evaluated settings, improves upon available neural decoding results.

title: Sharp Projection Bounds for Intermediate Dimensions of Measures
abstract: We prove sharp bounds for the upper and lower intermediate dimensions of orthogonal and radial projections of compactly supported measures. Both dimension functions are preserved almost everywhere when the quasi-Assouad dimension does not exceed the target dimension. We obtain exceptional-set estimates using the entire source dimension function, with sharpness for explicit families. We also construct a fixed measure whose projected dimension functions vary on open direction sets, even when all source dimensions lie below the target dimension.

title: Joint Angular-Power Distributions of Interfering Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
abstract: Finite populations of supermassive black-hole binaries produce fluctuations in both gravitational-wave power and pulsar timing correlations. We characterize the realization-dependent, orientation-averaged Earth-term angular correlation through its frequency-resolved Legendre coefficients. A hybrid model of bright sources and a Gaussian faint background extends the conditional Gamma distribution in the many-weak-source limit to non-central $χ^2$ statistics, yielding correlated multipoles after population marginalization. Our analytical variance decomposition and SMBHB population simulations reveal a population-dependent transition from interference dominated variance at low frequencies to population-power-dominated variance at high frequencies. In the many-weak-source regime, a multivariate lognormal approximation captures the main features of the joint distribution using only the first two log-cumulants. These results provide statistical benchmarks for fluctuations in both the overall amplitude and angular structure of the realized correlation.

title: Numerical analysis of a Lax-Wendroff type lattice Boltzmann scheme for the advection equation
abstract: A linear monodimensional lattice Boltzmann scheme with three velocities tackling the advection equation is investigated. We prove that it is second-order accurate and provide necessary and sufficient stability conditions through an explicit formula involving the two relaxation parameters. Relying on existing results for finite difference schemes, we prove convergence for smooth initial data with initialization of the non-conserved moments at equilibrium. Several numerical simulations illustrate these theoretical findings.

title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
abstract: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.

title: Exploiting the Weyl-Chamber Structure for Hardware-Aware Quantum Circuit Compression
abstract: Quantum circuit compression based on tensor networks enables long-time simulation of quantum many-body dynamics on near-term hardware. While Riemannian optimization has been successfully employed for this purpose, it typically optimizes over the manifold of generic two-qubit unitaries. Consequently, the resulting gates must still be synthesized into the hardware's native gate set via KAK decomposition, an overhead that partially negates the original compression gain. We show that Riemannian-optimized gates already exhibit a predictable Weyl structure: near-$R_{ZZ}$ for the Ising model and near-fSim for the Heisenberg XXZ model. Building on this insight, we investigate whether parameterized optimization directly over the native gate set can offer a beneficial trade-off between expressivity and circuit efficiency by reducing the circuit's dimensionality. When comparing the two approaches, we find that the small residual Weyl parameters neglected by the latter are essential for high compression of the Ising propagator, whereas for the Heisenberg propagator, the native XXZ structure can be exploited directly to build a more efficient compressed circuit.

title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
abstract: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
abstract: We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/Γ$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also obtain quantitative pointwise equidistribution for Haar-almost every point on each full expanding horosphere.

title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
abstract: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$α$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$α$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.

title: Sounding Surgical Instrument Localisation through Audio-Visual Correspondence
abstract: Surgical scene understanding is a prerequisite for context-aware and intelligent systems in the operating room. Current methods rely mostly on visual data, while acoustic sensing has shown potential to provide complementary information on surgical activity. First approaches for the localisation of surgical activity relied on microphone arrays and acoustic beamforming. This work investigates whether the active instrument can be localized from a single microphone and a camera by learning the correspondence between the appearance and the sound of surgical instruments, without annotating its position. We adapt weakly supervised audio-visual localisation, which learns from the co-occurrence of image and sound, to the surgical setting. We record simulated surgical actions, sawing, drilling, and chiseling, and train the model on these recordings without any spatial annotation to produce a heatmap over the sounding tool. We extend the training objective by two terms: a silence term, which suppresses the output for silence and background noise, and a composite term, which trains the model to select the sounding one of two visible instruments. The model localizes the active instrument on an independent corpus recorded with a different camera and microphone, in which instrument positions were obtained by optical tracking. It separates tool activity from silence and background noise and can attribute sound correctly when two tools are present. Audio-visual correspondence learned from in-domain recordings connects the sound of a surgical action to the instrument that produces it, using a single microphone and a camera. This proof of concept introduces a novel paradigm that enables the detection and localisation of surgical activity without manual annotations.

title: KrishokTech: A Bengali Agricultural Advisory System with Explicit Authorization Controls
abstract: For agricultural advisory, generating an answer is only part of the problem: the system must also control unsafe requests, work with limited connectivity, and accommodate changing guidance. KRISHOKTECH is a Bengali agricultural advisory system built around an explicit authorization boundary around generation. Before retrieval, normalization and rule-based admission checks refer policy-covered high-risk requests and ask for a crop when treatment intent is underspecified. The system then binds retrieval to a single crop and asks for confirmation when the text and image indicate different crops. After generation, a narrow verifier removes dosage claims not supported by retrieved BARI/BRRI evidence. Agricultural guidance is kept in an external evidence index that can be updated without retraining the generator, while browser-side vision and local retrieval reduce connectivity requirements. The interface makes these decisions visible as ASK, CONFIRM, REFER, and DROP, together with their evidence. On 200 farmer queries and 400 stress queries, the controls halted underspecified requests and reduced cross-crop retrieval violations from 36.5% to 0% under the tested alias filter. Mismatch detection caught 453 of 454 text-image conflicts, while the verifier caught 114 of 118 inserted dosage errors. The demonstration shows how these controls govern the path from request to delivered advice.

title: Logarithmic Separation between LZ77 and LZ-End and Grammar Compression
abstract: We show that there is a logarithmic separation between LZ77 and LZ-End, and between LZ77 and grammar compression.

title: Instability of mean curvature flow in expander coordinates
abstract: We study rotationally symmetric graphical solutions to mean curvature flow that are initially close to a homothetic reference expander, in particular near infinity. Based on a computer algebra aided proof, we show that under appropriate conditions, at large times, the solutions are closer to a different expander than to the reference expander.

title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
abstract: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+α}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

title: The boosted loop-erased random walk
abstract: We consider a near-critical version of loop-erased random walk (LERW) by boosting the weight of the underlying random walk according to its length before loop-erasure. We construct the scaling limit in natural parametrization in the two-dimensional unit disk and the three-dimensional unit ball. The boosted scaling limit undergoes a phase transition in mutual absolute continuity with the classical LERW scaling limit; in the disk the transition occurs at boost rate $m^2=π^2/4$. As the boost increases, the curve becomes macroscopically space-filling, in the sense that unvisited cubes have side length $O(m^{-1})$, while its Hausdorff dimension at each finite boost is unchanged. These results are motivated by Makarov--Smirnov's questions on near-critical lattice models. In the planar chordal setting, we also construct a continuum loop tilt below the spectral threshold of the domain and calculate its Loewner driving function.

title: On the Limits of Sparse Linear Model with Shuffled Differential Privacy
abstract: Sparse linear regression is a fundamental problem in high-dimensional statistics, and its private counterparts leave a large gap between the central and the local model of differential privacy. Shuffled differential privacy (SDP) sits between the two, offering accuracy closer to the central model without the trust requirement of a central curator. This paper studies sparse linear regression under both non-interactive and interactive SDP protocols. In the non-interactive setting, any non-interactive $(ε,δ)$-SDP protocol is shown to incur an $\ell_2$-norm estimation error of $Ω( \frac{\sqrt{dk}}{nε} )$ with dimension $d$, sparsity $k$, and $n$ users, revealing an inherent dimensionality barrier. In addition, a non-interactive algorithm is proposed that achieves an $\ell_2$-norm upper bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{n}} + \frac{d\sqrt{k}}{nε})$. To overcome this barrier, we turn to the interactive user-level setting, where each user holds $m$ samples. A two-round interactive algorithm is developed that first recovers the support through a heavy hitter step and then estimates the parameter, achieving an error of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{nm}} + \frac{k}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ with no polynomial dependence on $d$. Furthermore, by extending the score attack framework to user-level data, a new lower bound $Ω( \sqrt{\frac{k\log(d/k)}{nm}} + \frac{k\log(d/k)}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ is established for any user-level $(ε,δ)$-DP, showing that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal with only a gap of the factor $\log(d/k)$.

title: Minimal unitary representations of time-invariant causal quantum channels
abstract: In this work, we study quantum channels that respect causality in single-input-single-output linear time-invariant systems. We show that positive semidefinite kernels satisfying certain analyticity constraints, which we call Schur-class kernels, provide a suitable description of such channels through multiplicative maps (Schur multipliers). Using the Moore-Aronszajn Theorem, we establish that these multipliers admit a minimal analytic Stinespring representation, which, in the unital case, is given by multiplication by a left inner function. We then relate the output rank of pure-state inputs to the dimension of the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space. Using de Branges-Rovnyak realizations, we derive a stability criterion for the existence of two-sided inner completions of these vector-valued functions. We further show that the adjoint of the Julia embedding associated with the realization is minimal, and that its characteristic function essentially coincides with the canonical two-sided inner completion suggested by the Beurling-Lax-Halmos Theorem. Finally, we provide algorithms for explicitly computing minimal two-sided inner completions in the case of finite McMillan degree.

title: A Short Proof of Zhang's Conjecture on Stack-Sortable Permutations
abstract: We give a short proof of Zhang's conjecture that the number of stack-sortable permutations of length $n + 1$ which end in their smallest element is equal to the $n$-th Motzkin number.

title: Traces of Green's functions on $\mathbb{H}^q$ over point-hypersurface pairs
abstract: The famous algebraicity conjecture of Gross and Zagier for the values at CM points of higher Green's functions was recently proven by Bruinier, Li and Yang. Motivated by this the values of the automorphic Green's function at pairs of special points in hyperbolic $3$-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ were studied by Herrero, Imamoglu, von Pippich and Schwagenscheidt, and an analogous algebraicity result for traces of Green's functions was established. In this paper, we consider higher automorphic Green's functions $G_{s}(P,Q)$ on hyperbolic $q$-space $\mathbb{H}^q$ for $q\geq 2$ when the spectral parameter $s$ is a positive even integer, and prove an explicit finite formula for their traces over geodesic hypersurfaces in one of the variables. This formula provides a geometric interpretation of the traces of Green's functions for every choice of a point in $\mathbb{H}^q$ for the second variable. As an application, we obtain rationality results when the second variable is evaluated at a special point providing further evidence that such results for traces of Green's functions do not depend on any underlying complex structure.

title: Research of signs of star formation in three S0 galaxies - members of isolated pairs
abstract: We obtained and analyzed long-slit spectra of three lenticular galaxies with optical rings: PGC 48114, ESO 234-011, and ESO 444-076. Ionized gas was detected in all of them.
